articles.title: I really wanted to love the new Dell XPS 13, but Dell, we need to have a serious chat about your RAM choices
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Positioned as a rival to Apple's new budget-friendly MacBook Neo, the Dell XPS 13 returns for 2026 with an all-new design and lower price point. It's a bold move, and while Dell doesn't quite stick the landing, the end result is still a solid choice of laptop for anyone who prefers Windows over macOS. Battery life and display quality are great, and the all-metal chassis feels durable, if a bit less flashy than previous models. However, it falls down a little when it comes to pricing, and the base configuration is somewhat underpowered, further compounding the price issue.
Pros
- +Thin but sturdy chassis
- +Great display
- +Performance is solid (though unspectacular)
- +Strong battery life
Cons
- -Poor port selection
- -8GB of RAM in base configuration is insufficient
- -Non-US pricing situation is dire
Why you can trust TechRadar
Dell XPS 13 (2026): Two-minute review
The new Dell XPS 13 (2026) is a shift from Dell's usual modus operandi, finally bringing the premium-quality XPS line down to a more affordable space. If that sounds familiar, it's because Apple did the exact same thing earlier this year: the arrival of the MacBook Neo has shaken up the laptop market, and evidently left other manufacturers scrambling to front their own competition to Apple's new wallet-friendly MacBook.
But before I delve into how effective a frontline soldier Dell's new effort is in the never-ending battle between Windows and Mac, it's time for a brief history lesson: the lore of XPS, if you like.
Dell's XPS brand was unceremoniously killed off last year, before being suddenly resurrected at CES 2026, presumably because their executives realised that shuttering your single most iconic and well-loved brand is a bad idea (shocker, I know). But as I mentioned above, the return of XPS has seen a paradigm shift; while the Dell XPS 14 and XPS 16 are still the pricey, high-end laptops I've come to expect from the XPS lineup, the new XPS 13 is an entirely different beast.
It's still identifiably an XPS laptop, there's no denying that. From the ultra-thin chassis to the all-metal casing and minimalist logo on the lid, you'd be forgiven for thinking at first glance that this was just another premium XPS model.
But opening up the laptop betrays its more budget-conscious nature immediately; gone are the giant, edgeless touchpad and zero-spacing keyboard seen on this year's 14- and 16-inch models, replaced instead by more traditional fare. The touchpad and keyboard here wouldn't look out of place on the average Chromebook.
A peek at the spec sheet further solidifies the new XPS 13's position as a MacBook Neo rival; a lower-end hexa-core Intel Core 5 chip and only 8GB of RAM in the base model all point to this being a more sensibly priced product.
I'll dig into the performance specifics later in this review, but the good news is that the lower-spec hardware doesn't render the XPS 13 dangerously underpowered. This laptop is perfectly capable of handling everyday work, even if it's not a performant powerhouse like its bigger siblings. The battery life is also excellent, and the display is very high quality for the price point. In short, there's a lot to love here.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Unfortunately, there are a few things that hold this new breed of XPS back. The base configuration features only 8GB of RAM, which is fundamentally insufficient in the current era of Windows software, and the measly port selection may prove frustrating for some users. It's also just a bit too expensive to be considered a true rival to the MacBook Neo.
Now, it's arguable that this isn't entirely Dell's fault. The ongoing RAM crisis, spurred by skyrocketing demand for AI data center hardware, is causing the prices of all kinds of computer components to spike sharply. Shifting to 8GB of RAM in the base configuration is very likely to be a cost-saving move. Overall, I'd say that this is a pretty solid effort from Dell – just don't expect too much from it.
Dell XPS 13 (2026) review: Price & availability
- Starts at $699 / £749 / AU$1,597.20
- Student discounts help a lot
- Available worldwide
Brace yourself: this is going to be one of the longest price sections I've written for a review in a while. There's a lot to talk about here, sorry!
Apologies to our readers outside the US: the pricing of the Dell XPS 13 beyond America is pretty damn awful, to the point where I'm worried it might have already scuppered any chance of this laptop being a genuine competitor against the MacBook Neo.
In the US, the base configuration comes with a 256GB SSD, Intel Core 5 320 processor, and 8GB of RAM. It'll cost you a very reasonable $699, or $599 with a student discount – in other words, exactly the same price as the 256GB MacBook Neo.
However, I'd generally struggle a little to recommend that version. 8GB of RAM is simply substandard for running software in Windows 11 these days, especially if you plan to run multiple programs at once. Stepping up to the safer recommended 16GB of RAM (which also mandatorily bumps up the SSD to 512GB) will cost you $899, already taking us a fair bit beyond the competing MacBook Neo. Of course, there's no 16GB version of the Neo available, but it's worth noting that the 'unified memory' used by Apple's laptops is a bit more efficient than traditional laptop RAM.
Outside the US, things start to look dicey. For starters, there's no 256GB SSD configuration available in Australia, with the cheapest available models starting at £749 / AU$1,597.20 – a far less attractive prospect after accounting for exchange rates. And if you want to bump things up to 16GB of RAM, you're looking at a fairly steep £1,099 / $1,897.50. My review unit is the 8GB UK configuration with 512GB of storage, which will cost you £899 (though at the time of writing, it's already on sale for £769)
There are higher-spec models available, too, with the RAM configurable up to 32GB and the SSD up to 1TB, as well as the option to upgrade the CPU to a significantly more powerful Intel Core Ultra 7 355. This top-spec model will cost you $1,799.99 / £1,899 / $3,698.20 – and quite frankly, at that point you might be better served by opting for the more premium XPS 14. Configurations with the Core Ultra 7 processor also benefit from an upgrade to Thunderbolt 4-capable USB-C ports.
Overall, I'm not too impressed by the pricing of the Dell XPS 13, especially considering its market position as a Windows-toting rival to the MacBook Neo. There's certainly still an argument that it deserves a place among the best budget laptops (for buyers in the US, at least), but it's not the phenomenal value product I was really hoping to see when I first heard about it. Still, if you're a US shopper who wants a basic but effective laptop for work or school, it's not a terrible choice.
- Value score: 3 / 5
Dell XPS 13 (2026) review: Specs
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | Base spec | Max spec | 
| Price | $699 / £749 / AU$1,597.20 | $1,799.99 / £1,899 / $3,698.20 | 
| CPU | Intel Core 5 320 | Intel Core Ultra 7 355 | 
| Graphics | Integrated Intel Graphics | Integrated Intel Graphics | 
| RAM | 8GB LPDDR5X | 32GB LPDDR5X | 
| Display | 13.4inch, 2.5K (2560 x 1440), 120Hz, 500 nits, Touch | 13.4inch, 2.5K (2560 x 1440), 120Hz, 500 nits, Touch | 
| Storage | 256GB M.2 PCIe SSD | 1TB M.2 PCIe SSD | 
| Ports and Connectivity | 2x USB-C 3.2 Gen 2; Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 | 2x Thunderbolt 4 USB-C; Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 | 
| Battery | 52Wh | 52Wh | 
| Weight | 2.2lbs (1 kg) | 2.2lbs (1 kg) | 
| Dimensions | 11.7 x 7.9 x 0.5 inches / 297 x 201 x 13mm | 11.7 x 7.9 x 0.5 inches / 297 x 201 x 13mm | 
Dell XPS 13 (2026) review: Design
- Impressively thin and light
- Premium build quality
- Port selection is feeble
Straight off the bat, despite its aggressive redesign and shift towards more conventional aesthetics, the 2026 Dell XPS 13 still feels like a premium product. I might have complained about the pricing further up in this review, but considering that the build quality remains solid regardless of which configuration you buy, I have to admit that I'm very pleased here.
The entire chassis is machined from high-grade aluminum, making it highly durable without compromising on weight. The whole thing weighs almost exactly one kilogram, and combined with the 13.4-inch display's slim bezels, it's a very portable laptop indeed.
It's also impressively thin, measuring just half an inch thick with the lid closed. The casing has rounded corners and a smooth matte finish, which is reasonably good at resisting scratches and fingerprint marks. It's available in a few different colorways, all muted metallic tones, with availability varying between regions and configurations.
The keyboard and touchpad are totally different from what we've seen on previous XPS 13 models, now trending towards functionality over style. The LED-backlit keys are reasonably spaced, comfortable to type on even for extended periods, and have a decent amount of travel despite the laptop's ultra-thin design.
They're perhaps a little spongy on full presses for my liking, with a bit of flex in the keyboard housing; something which I consider completely forgivable in a sub-$800 laptop, but might push some users towards the more premium typing experience of the XPS 14 or 16. Similarly, the touchpad has a satisfying click, but firm presses on the bottom corners feel a tiny bit flimsy – definitely not a dealbreaker for a budget laptop, but again, it gives me pause when it comes to recommending the higher-spec models.
Thankfully, some things haven't changed from previous models. The display is once again the star of the show here: a fantastic 2.5K touch panel, boasting good maximum brightness and impressive color reproduction, especially considering that the screen is the same regardless of which internal spec you opt for. If you get the cheapest configuration, you're getting plenty of bang for your buck when it comes to the display.
Looking at the rest of the physical design, it's all good without being spectacular. The speakers are integrated under thin slots on either side of the base and are reasonably loud for such a small laptop. Don't expect thumping bass here, but the volume is good without high notes sounding tinny.
The webcam is also decent, 1080p rather than the 720p resolution you'll find on many budget-conscious laptops. I've certainly seen sharper webcam footage, and the low-light performance is merely okay, but it gets the job done well for the most part. It also supports facial recognition logins via Windows Hello. The integrated microphone array is decidedly average, though, so I'd advise getting a decent headset if you plan to make regular video calls.
Lastly, we come to connectivity, which is perhaps the most mixed part of an already mixed bag. Wireless connectivity is top-notch; Wi-Fi 7 ensures speedy, lossless internet (assuming you're connected to a network that supports it!) while Bluetooth 6.0 is an exceedingly rare sight on any laptop under $1,000.
Physical connections, though? Yeah, this one's a wash. We criticised the MacBook Neo for only having two basic USB-C ports (no Thunderbolt 4 support), and it's the same case here. Granted, these are both USB 3.2, while one of the Neo's ports is a frankly pathetic USB 2, and springing for the higher-spec CPU upgrades both ports to Thunderbolt 4, but it's still just fundamentally not enough ports.
Considering that the only way to charge the XPS 13 is to use one of the only two ports available, you're down to just a single port any time it's plugged in. Power users who want to connect multiple peripherals are going to need to spend extra on a USB-C hub, and anyone who doesn't shell out for the more powerful CPU will be dealing with slower charging and data transfer speeds.
Overall, it's a well-designed laptop that feels like it should last for years, but I will be docking a point for the sheer dearth of ports. If you prefer to connect your hardware solely via wireless means, though, you should have very little to complain about here.
- Design score: 4 / 5
Dell XPS 13 (2026) review: Performance
- Decent everyday performance
- Gets a little warm under load
- 8GB RAM is simply not enough for heavier workloads

Total War: Warhammer III: 1080p, Medium: N/A
Total War: Warhammer III: 1800p, Ultra: N/A
Battery Life (TechRadar movie test): 16 hours and 17 minutes
I'm a big believer in setting realistic expectations, so once I learned that my XPS 13 review unit was the UK standard configuration with 8GB of RAM and the decidedly low-end Core Ultra 5 320 CPU, I immediately tempered my hopes of great performance.
Despite this, this XPS 13 performed a bit better than I'd expected overall. Performance in my everyday workloads – including web browsing, word processing, and some light image editing in GIMP – was good, with virtually no slowdown even with half a dozen Chrome tabs open and Spotify running in the background. Windows 11 generally felt snappy and responsive.
The more you start to load it down with tasks, though, the more it struggles. The simple fact is that in the current age of computer software, 8GB of RAM just isn't sufficient for more complex or varied workloads.
It was a telling moment when Apple finally relented and upgraded the minimum starting memory on the best MacBooks to 16GB rather than 8GB back in 2024; the demands of modern professionals have shifted, and I was rather upset to see that the MacBook Neo has reverted back to 8GB as standard. However, this is less of a problem for Apple, since the 'unified memory' used in MacBooks is faster and more efficient than traditional DDR laptop RAM, and the company's total control of the Mac software/hardware ecosystem makes optimizing for less memory a bit easier.
So let's break down how the XPS 13's 8GB of RAM actually performed. I'll start with the bad news: some of my tests failed to complete altogether, loading up but then aborting. I've not seen this happen in quite a while, with the 16GB industry standard evidently shielding me from such failures.
In total, the XPS 13 failed eight of our standard benchmark tests, most of which were the more demanding 3DMark graphical tests. However, I also noticed some instability in other tests; Cinebench crashed several times before I was able to get stable readings, and 3DMark also crashed once before I was even able to start running tests.
The tests that did run showed decidedly lackluster performance in 3D rendering and similar creative workloads. This isn't a laptop you'll be squeezing in a few rounds of Marvel Rivals on, though I did manage to get Slay the Spire II running fine, so perhaps some 2D indie gaming is still on the table here.
Outside of regular testing, I also tried to fire up Adobe Photoshop and Premiere Pro. Both initially loaded without crashing, but were sluggish in practice, and Photoshop ended up crashing after about five minutes of use.
The Dell XPS 13 (2026) got rather warm during the more intensive tests. The thermal exhaust is a thin slot nestled into the display hinge, and while the fans remained impressively quiet throughout my testing, the underside of the laptop did get too toasty to comfortably have it actually on your lap while running resource-intensive software. It did remain cool and near-silent during regular office work, however.
The takeaway here is that while the 8GB model of the XPS 13 is perfectly capable of handling basic everyday workloads, it just doesn't have the oomph for anything more demanding than straightforward office or schoolwork. If that's all you want to do, the budget-friendly 8GB configuration should be fine; if you've got grander designs than that, you'll need to pay extra for a more powerful model.
- Performance score: 3 / 5
Dell XPS 13 (2026) review: Battery life
Intel's third-generation Core chips are clearly putting in some work here. Although the Dell XPS 13 (2026) only has a 52Wh battery (far smaller than the batteries you'll find on many ultrabooks these days), the efficiency of this chip can't be understated; our video playback battery test saw the laptop sail comfortably past the 16-hour mark.
There are laptops that can go for longer, but at this price point, that's a very respectable effort. It outstrips the MacBook Neo by nearly three hours according to our tests. I found that even at maximum brightness, with a Bluetooth mouse and headset connected and the Windows power mode set to Balanced, it could comfortably make it through an eight-hour workday without needing a charge.
The laptop also holds charge fantastically when not in use. My partner got sick, and I had to shelve this review for a couple of weeks, during which time the XPS 13 simply sat untouched on a desk in my home office. When I finally opened it up to start my review process, it was still at 90% charge. When plugged in, it charges up to full in just under an hour (though the higher-spec model with Thunderbolt 4 ports will presumably charge faster).
My only real criticism here is that it doesn't come with a power adapter in the UK and EU. Much like Apple's approach with the MacBook Neo, this is ostensibly due to local regulations that mandate consumers' ability to buy a laptop without a charger, but come on; you could include the option to add one at checkout. I've criticized Apple for this in the past, too: it's malicious compliance, and it's simply irritating for the end user.
- Battery life score: 4.5 / 5
Should I buy the Dell XPS 13?
Scorecard
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | The UK and Australia pricing is a shame, but student discounts help a lot, and the base model is very reasonable in the US. | 3 / 5 | 
| Design | Despite a disappointing port selection, this is a well-crafted laptop that feels nicely durable and packs an excellent touch display. | 4 / 5 | 
| Performance | Decent performance in everyday tasks, but users aiming to multitask will definitely want to invest in the 16GB RAM model. | 3 / 5 | 
| Battery life | The XPS 13 can comfortably cruise through a full workday (and then some) without needing a charge. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Total Score | The 2026 XPS 13 isn't quite the MacBook Neo-beater that Dell clearly hoped it would be, but it's still a solid pick for anyone who wants a Windows alternative to Apple's new budget MacBook. | 3.65 / 5 | 
Buy it if…
You want something ultra-portable
The impressively slim design, one-kilo total weight, and sturdy aluminum chassis all work together to make the XPS 13 an eminently portable laptop for taking on the go.
You want a premium design for a non-premium price
It looks and feels impressively high-end, even in the cheapest available configurations. While it might be a little more function-over-form than the larger XPS models, this still feels like a premium laptop.
Don't buy it if…
You want lots of ports
There are only two ports on board, and both are USB-C (without Thunderbolt 4 in our review configuration), so you'll need a USB hub if you want to connect multiple peripherals.
You want to run demanding software
While it can handle everyday work with easy, the lower-end CPU and 8GB of RAM in the base configuration simply don't offer enough juice for power users planning on aggressive multitasking or resource-intensive programs.
Dell XPS 13 (2026) review: Also consider
HP OmniBook 7 14-inch (2025)
Like the XPS 13, the OmniBook 7 is an incredibly thin and light laptop. Not only that, our reviewer was very impressed with how well it handled all kinds of workloads, and it has a superb battery life to boot. Read our full HP OmniBook 7 14-inch (2025) review.
Asus Zenbook A14
Another ultra-portable hero, the A14 offers truly staggering battery life; in fact, it’s the most enduring laptop we've tested in recent years, lasting a staggering 28 hours in our movie playback test. Its build isn’t as premium as the XPS 13’s, and its display isn’t as bright, but it’s still a capable machine. Read our full Asus Zenbook A14 review.
How I tested the Dell XPS 13 (2026)
- Tested for one week
- Used for a variety of workloads
- 8+ years of hardware testing experience
If you've read any of my other reviews, you'll already know the drill: I swapped out my daily driver (the excellent Asus Zenbook Duo 14) for the Dell XPS 13 for one full week, including the weekend.
This helps me get a proper feeling for how the laptop functions in everyday use scenarios, testing it out for a range of typical tasks including web research, writing articles, and image editing. Naturally, I also ran the laptop through our usual suite of synthetic benchmarking tests, including our looped video test for battery life.
I've been a computer hardware journalist for more than eight years, and working for TechRadar for half a decade. In that time, I've reviewed more laptops than I can remember for numerous different publications; the number is certainly in the dozens, quite likely into triple digits by now! I put every bit of experience and expertise I've gained over those years into my reviews, so you can rest assured that you're getting accurate, bias-free information.
- First reviewed: September 2026
- Read more about how we test
Christian is TechRadar’s UK-based Computing Editor. He came to us from Maximum PC magazine, where he fell in love with computer hardware and building PCs. He was a regular fixture amongst our freelance review team before making the jump to TechRadar, and can usually be found drooling over the latest high-end graphics card or gaming laptop before looking at his bank account balance and crying.
Christian is a keen campaigner for LGBTQ+ rights and the owner of a charming rescue dog named Lucy, having adopted her after he beat cancer in 2021. She keeps him fit and healthy through a combination of face-licking and long walks, and only occasionally barks at him to demand treats when he’s trying to work from home.

articles.title: The Reconfigurable Analog Front End - EE Times
articles.text:
Reuse Forever? Ok, maybe that’s a stretch, but that is the profile of design engineers who use GreenPAKTM products. Typically, when an engineer designs with a GreenPAK product, they use it repeatedly due to the many advantages it offers, including reconfigurability. This addresses the proverbial “work smarter” and “not harder” mantra we all hear from our bosses.
If you are not familiar with GreenPAK, it is a family of configurable hardware devices that integrate many system functions into a single custom circuit, and in the process, minimizes cost, complexity, component count, board space, power consumption, and development time.
There are different categories of the GreenPAK products that integrate macrocells or functions such as Power, High Voltage, and Analog to address a wide range of application use cases. One of the newer categories of the GreenPAK family is AnalogPAK TM, which integrates both analog and digital capabilities. Think of it as an autonomous, configurable analog front end that essentially behaves like an analog ASIC.
The analog world behaves differently than the digital world. There are many variables that need to be considered when designing robust analog circuits. That is why analog designers become creatures of habit. They reuse what they trust: a favorite op amp, a proven ADC, a reference circuit that consistently meets noise, bandwidth and stability targets.
Many analog-centric or sensor-centric systems partition their design into analog and digital sections. The analog section tends to be reused either across multiple platforms or through multiple generations. The digital section tends to be updated more frequently to address different features across products, more communication bandwidth needed in the system, or more demands placed on the processing and control capability of the system.
Imagine if you suddenly had the ability to configure and scale your analog design in a similar fashion to configuring and scaling digital design without the need for hardware or software upgrades or consuming any additional MCU resources. That is where the AnalogPAK products come into play.
AnalogPAK: A Marriage Made in Silicon Heaven
Some marriages just work. Partners in those marriages balance each other’s strengths and weaknesses, divide responsibilities more naturally, more easily deal with adversity due to each partner’s perspective, and overcome obstacles by leaning into each other’s strengths when needed.
AnalogPAK is an example of marriage between analog and digital that just works. It makes use of the flexibility and reusability of the GreenPAK family by combining configurable analog and digital functionality to address a variety of solutions. This greatly expands the reuse and scalability of the product.
A common pain point in sensor-centric products is that the same hardware platform must support the same sensor over multiple ranges or even variations of sensors across different products. AnalogPAK can solve this problem more easily than other traditional analog design approaches.
The first example below illustrates the flexibility of the SLG47003 AnalogPAK with integrated operational amplifiers by supporting the same sensor over multiple ranges:
Example 1: Target sensor (one PCB, multiple ranges):
- Variable Current Shunt Measurement Range: 10 mA to 10 A (1000:1 dynamic range)
This design needs variable gain to meet the requirement of supporting different ranges in an application. Rather than solve the problem through a hardware solution by using different devices with fixed gain or different discrete components to create different gains, this solution uses the programmability of the device to dynamically change the amplifier gain to maximize the signal-to-noise ratio of the system. Furthermore, the analog comparators can be used to detect overrange conditions to indicate to the controlling device that the gain setting needs to be adjusted.
For the second example, suppose we want to support different sensors across different products. This example of a more complex design could support temperature measurement for thermistors, RTDs, thermocouples and also resistive bridge measurements from the same platform.
Example 2: Target sensors (one PCB, multiple variants):
- Thermistor module: wide input range. Non-linear transfer function that requires linearization. Low bandwidth and low noise sensitivity.
- RTD module: wide input range. Non-linear transfer function that requires linearization. Low bandwidth and medium noise sensitivity.
- Thermocouple module: low input range. Non-linear transfer function that requires linearization. Low bandwidth and high noise sensitivity.
- Resistive Bridge Sensor module: wide input range with analog output. Non-linear transfer function that requires linearization. Low bandwidth and high noise sensitivity.
The design example uses the SLG47011 AnalogPAK with integrated analog and digital features. To simplify the analog circuit design, the example utilizes voltage biasing, the programmable gain amplifier to support different analog input voltage ranges, an adjustable sampling frequency to accommodate the different bandwidth and noise requirements, and the memory table and math core to compensate for the non-linearity of the sensors.
The shared requirements for all modules reuse the same analog PCB across variants, maintain predictable measurement behavior, support range changes (gain), noise/latency tradeoffs (filtering/averaging), and optional alarm thresholds without adding ICs or re-spinning resistor networks.
SLG47011 key features for the configurable analog front end:
- Programmable Gain Amplifier (PGA): sets gain to map the active sensor range into the ADC input range without changing precision resistors on the PCB.
- SAR ADC acquisition: samples the conditioned signal with deterministic timing; option to buffer or stream results to a host when needed.
- Averaging/oversampling reduces noise or increases effective resolution by adjusting averaging depth (trading response time vs. noise) in configured hardware.
- Linearization (memory-table y = f(x)): applies a lookup-based transfer function for non-linear resistive sensors without SW or piecewise compensation methods.
- Window comparator + hysteresis: implement programmable high/low thresholds for over-temp, over-current, or out-of-range detection with hysteresis behavior.
- Outputs: assert a digital fault, generate PWM/DAC proportional output, or report digital samples over I2C/SPI depending on system needs.
What changes between variants is the configuration, but not the board. Each module supports different input channel selection, adjustable PGA gain, choice of averaging depth, loading a different linearization table, and updating comparator thresholds.
Signal Conditioner for a Pressure Sensor 
Thermocouple Cold Junction Compensation
Side Bar: Scalability of the SLG47011
I Now Pronounce You an Analog Engineer
The problems with analog design are often not specific to one particular device – they are architectural. The SLG47011 is compelling because it shifts key mixed-signal behavior from an engineered by trial-and-error approach to a design that is consistent by configuration. This is why engineers who adopt it once often reuse it again.
The advantages of the SLG47011 include:
1) Deterministic behavior because it is configuration-defined
In an MCU-centric architecture, analog performance is dependent upon code execution and timing, clock synchronization, bus traffic, interrupt handling and timing and power-state changes. With the SLG47011, the sampling, buffering, math/linearization, and thresholding can be implemented in configured hardware blocks. That makes key behavior more repeatable across revisions and operating modes, which directly reduces debug time and version dependent performance surprises.
2) Designs are built from reusable “modules,” not re-invented
Just like designers “go to” analog components, designers will use a set of proven  
Go Configure TM project “modules” that can be reused with minor parameter changes. These include: 
- Acquisition front end: PGA setup + ADC timing + data buffer configuration including averaging or oversampling.
- Linearization: memory-table transfer functions for sensors with non-linear curves.
- Decision logic: digital comparator thresholds (with hysteresis) for windowing, alarms, or multi-level state changes.
- Signal generation: DAC/PWM outputs for control loops, LED drive patterns, or “analog-out” conversion from processed measurements.
- Sequencing: counters/delays and configurable logic for deterministic timing without the MCU having to manage synchronization.
3) Validation becomes more predictable
Because the SLG47011’s mixed-signal behavior is defined by a configuration that can be emulated and tested early, teams can validate timing, filtering, and thresholds before committing to a final board design. This tends to shrink the “unknowns” that usually drive extra prototype spins and reduces the burden of proving that an update did not subtly change measurement behavior.
4) Familiarity compounds: the same flow applies across very different applications
The SLG47011 is one of those devices where the second project is materially easier than the first. Once an engineer understands the macrocells (ADC + buffers + math + memory table + digital logic) and the Go Configure workflow, that same skill transfers to many problem domains – from sensor interfaces to power monitoring to protocol/control logic. Over time, designers accumulate internal reference designs, test setups, and known-good configurations, creating a reusable design for future products.
A Practical Design Workflow for AnalogPAK That Scales For New Designs
- Start with the signal chain: define sensor type, expected input range, required bandwidth, and accuracy targets (noise/ENOB, thresholds, response time).
- Map functions to on-chip blocks: decide what lives inside the SLG47011 (gain, sampling, averaging/oversampling, linearization, thresholding, control outputs) versus what remains external.
- Build the configuration in Go Configure: implement the acquisition and processing path using the device’s configurable blocks, then simulate and iterate.
- Prototype with an evaluation board: validate real signals and corner cases early (timing, noise coupling, temperature behavior).
- Freeze the design: once validated, treat the configuration like a controlled artifact (version it, document it, and reuse it).
- Create your internal “module library”: extract the acquisition and processing fragments that were successful and reuse them as starting points for the next project.
Conclusion
The strongest advantage of AnalogPAK products is that they turn mixed-signal performance from something teams continuously “engineer and defend” into something they can configure and reuse. That shift – deterministic acquisition, reusable processing modules, and a repeatable workflow – is why engineers who succeed with one SLG47011 design so often come back for the next one.

articles.title: Cargas a más de un megavatio: así es el revolucionario sistema que permite cargar camiones en cuestión de minutos
articles.text:
Tal y como ocurre con los vehículos de pasajeros, si se quiere fomentar el uso del camión eléctrico debe existir también una infraestructura de carga madura para que tenga sentido, y Europa es el parque de pruebas perfecto para las compañías. En este aspecto, la empresa especializada en infraestructura de carga Zerova ha presentado un sistema de carga a nivel de megavatio específico para camiones y autobuses eléctricos. La compañía mostró la unidad en el IAA Transportation de Hanóver, justo el evento en el que Tesla también anunció la llegada de su camión eléctrico Semi a Europa. Zerova afirma que su dispensador de cargasuministra hasta 1.440 kW y 1.500 A por unidad. Te contamos todos los detalles.
Carga de megavatio. Llegar a este nivel de potencia es una pieza clave para que el transporte pesado se pueda electrificar y pueda funcionar a gran escala. Un camión de larga distancia con una batería gigantesca no puede permitirse paradas largas, así que para eso hay que conseguir que el proceso de carga admita suministrar energía a mayor potencia.
Hasta ahora, Zerova ha sido conocida por sus sistemas de carga en cocheras y autobuses, y ahora quiere aprovechar que el sector del camión se está movilizando hacia la electrificación para deslumbrar con sus propuestas.
En detalle. El dispensador es una unidad “satélite”. Esto quiere decir que la electrónica de potencia permanece en un armario independiente, mientras que el dispensador es solo el punto de carga. Zerova lo construye sobre sus armarios de potencia DO360 y DZ480 existentes, que ofrecen una tensión de salida en corriente continua de 150-950 V y 200-950 V, respectivamente.
Por otro lado, merece la pena echarle un vistazo al resto de su apartado técnico:
- Cables: refrigerados por líquido, en longitudes de 5 o 7 metros, y equipados con un conector MCS o CCS2.
- Potencia: la cifra de 1.440 kW se aplica al conector MCS. Aunque en el anuncio no se indica la potencia máxima de la toma CCS.
- Interfaz: una pantalla táctil de 10,4 pulgadas con clasificación IK8.
- Pago y acceso: RFID, código QR y Plug & Charge, con un terminal de tarjeta opcional.
La empresa también afirma que la plataforma está diseñada para seguir el estándar CharIN MCS a medida que se desarrolle, tras la publicación de la especificación del conector IEC TS 63379 a principios de este año. Estas son dos piezas clave para traer la carga rápida a nivel de megavatio y estandarizarla a nivel mundial en camiones y otros vehículos pesados.
Diseño. Debido a que los armarios y los dispensadores están separados, un operador puede configurar una ubicación para la carga en cocheras o para un corredor y añadir capacidad más adelante. Así que su principal argumento de venta está precisamente en que es modular. Judy Hung, directora de Operaciones Comerciales de Zerova, cuenta que la plataforma está “diseñada para crecer junto al estándar MCS a medida que se consolide en toda Europa”. La propuesta está dirigida a operadores que desean instalar la carga de megavatios ahora, pero esperan que el mercado y el estándar sigan cambiando.
¿Y ahora qué? El dispensador se ha exhibido durante la IAA Transportation de Hanover. Ahora queda ver si Zerova detalla un poco más la parte de qué clientes acabarán optando por su sistema de carga y en qué emplazamientos se irán añadiendo sus conectores. Brian Huang, director general de Zerova Reino Unido, afirma que los operadores de cocheras y las flotas de logística en Europa están pidiendo una carga de clase megavatio que puedan desplegar hoy y ampliar mañana.

articles.title: "C'est du vent pour protéger leurs marges" : le patron d'Acer critique la spéculation sur la RAM et prédit la fin de la crise
articles.text:
La crise de la RAM pousse les prix toujours plus loin et toujours plus haut, mais vent contre tous, un homme, le PDG d'Acer, s'exprime clairement. Pour lui, les prix sont gonflés artificiellement et le seront jusqu'en 2030, alors qu'une porte de sortie de la crise actuelle devrait arriver prochainement.
Alors que plusieurs producteurs de semi-conducteurs anticipent des tensions d'approvisionnement jusqu'en 2030, le président-directeur général d'Acer, Jason Chen, prévoit un changement de tendance sur le marché des composants. Pour lui, dès fin 2027, les prix des ordinateurs devraient commencer à diminuer.
Une durée de pénuries à prédire
Le secteur des composants informatiques a connu d'importantes perturbations liées au développement de l'intelligence artificielle, débutant par les cartes graphiques à la fin de l'année 2022 avant de toucher la RAM à la fin de l'année 2025. Ces tensions ont entraîné une hausse de 500 % du prix des puces mémoire en l'espace de douze mois. Cette progression tend à se ralentir, les consommateurs arrêtant d'accepter d'être les dindons de la farce. Ainsi, les ventes de RAM au grand public ont largement chuté. Sans compter les contrefaçons à prix attractifs.
Des acteurs de l'industrie, comme l'entreprise SK hynix, avancent que la pénurie s'aggravera l'année prochaine et que les tarifs ne se normaliseront pas avant 2030. Le dirigeant de la société Adata a quant à lui évoqué un manque de mémoire DRAM pouvant s'étendre sur dix ans. Ces arguments s'appuient sur la demande soutenue en mémoires HBM de la part des acteurs de l'intelligence artificielle et sur le fait que les nouvelles usines de fabrication en construction ne seront pas opérationnelles avant la fin des années 2030.
Mais Jason Chen, PDG d'Acer, conteste cette grille de lecture. Selon lui, les principaux fournisseurs de mémoire cherchent à maintenir leurs marges brutes élevées le plus longtemps possible en orientant leurs messages vers une hausse des prix durable. Il affirme que l'offre en mémoires et en SSD est aujourd'hui suffisante et que les difficultés d'approvisionnement en processeurs se limitent à des modèles spécifiques. Seules des pièces haut de gamme comme la mémoire LPDDR5X-9600 ou les puces N1 et N1X de Nvidia restent actuellement rares.
Quels tarifs d'ici 2027 ?
En raison d'un décalage de quelques mois entre les tarifs appliqués par les fournisseurs et les prix publics, Jason Chen indique que le prix des ordinateurs augmentera encore de 5 % à 20 % d'ici la fin de cette année. Les tarifs devraient ensuite se stabiliser au cours du premier semestre 2027, avant d'amorcer une baisse.
Arrivée de puces chinoises et coût des sous-composants
Le patron d'Acer souligne également que l'émergence de fabricants chinois proposant des composants à bas coût vient perturber le marché, un facteur qui suscite des inquiétudes chez le président du groupe SK, Chey Tae-won. Des constructeurs comme Acer, HP et Asus intègrent désormais des puces de l'entreprise CXMT dans certains de leurs produits, tandis que des modèles de marque Lenovo vendus en Allemagne intègrent des SSD produits par YMTC.
En parallèle, Jason Chen observe que d'autres éléments subissent à leur tour des hausses de tarifs, notamment les circuits imprimés (PCB) et la toile de verre servant à la fabrication des cartes mères. Le responsable a exprimé son étonnement face aux demandes de revalorisation de prix formulées par les fournisseurs pour ces sous-composants.

articles.title: NVIDIA y AMD frenan sus nuevas GPU: la próxima generación no llegaría hasta 2028
articles.text:
Las próximas generaciones de tarjetas gráficas de NVIDIA y AMD podrían retrasarse hasta 2028, según información atribuida al conocido filtrador Kepler_L2. La previsión apunta a que ambas compañías reducirían durante 2027 sus lanzamientos de GPU destinadas al mercado de consumo, en un momento en el que la industria de los semiconductores está dando prioridad a los procesadores utilizados para inteligencia artificial (IA).
La información todavía no ha sido confirmada oficialmente por NVIDIA ni AMD. Por ahora, ninguna de las dos compañías ha anunciado un calendario definitivo para sus próximas arquitecturas de tarjetas gráficas destinadas a videojuegos.
PUBLICIDAD
La inteligencia artificial cambia las prioridades
El principal motivo señalado para este posible retraso es el crecimiento de la demanda de hardware para IA. Los centros de datos necesitan grandes cantidades de aceleradores especializados para entrenar y ejecutar modelos de inteligencia artificial, un mercado que genera importantes ingresos para los fabricantes de chips.
Según la información de Kepler_L2, esta situación estaría llevando a NVIDIA y AMD a priorizar la producción destinada a servidores y servicios de computación en la nube frente a las tarjetas gráficas para jugadores.
La fabricación de estos componentes también compite por recursos con las GPU de consumo. La disponibilidad limitada de memoria y otros componentes, junto con el aumento de los costes de producción, habría complicado todavía más la planificación de nuevos modelos.
PUBLICIDAD
NVIDIA podría concentrarse en la siguiente generación
En el caso de NVIDIA, las filtraciones apuntan a que la compañía podría retrasar o incluso cancelar la renovación intermedia de su actual familia de tarjetas gráficas.
La serie RTX 50 SUPER, que se había rumoreado como una actualización de la generación actual, habría perdido prioridad debido a las condiciones del mercado. La compañía podría concentrar recursos en su siguiente gran salto arquitectónico, que según estas informaciones correspondería a la futura familia RTX 60.
Si este escenario se confirma, los jugadores podrían pasar 2027 sin una renovación completa de la gama de NVIDIA y tendrían que esperar hasta 2028 para encontrar una nueva generación de tarjetas gráficas.
PUBLICIDAD
AMD mantendría una excepción en 2027
AMD también estaría preparando una estrategia similar para sus próximas GPU basadas en la arquitectura RDNA 5. Sin embargo, las filtraciones señalan una posible excepción.
La compañía podría lanzar en 2027 una tarjeta identificada con el nombre en clave AT2, situada en la gama media-alta. El modelo tendría 40 unidades de cómputo y utilizaría 12 GB de memoria GDDR7 mediante un bus de 192 bits.
Esta GPU buscaría competir con modelos actuales de mayor rendimiento, entre ellos la GeForce RTX 5080. Sería, de acuerdo con la información filtrada, el único lanzamiento relevante de AMD basado en RDNA 5 durante 2027.
PUBLICIDAD
Las versiones de mayor rendimiento quedarían para 2028, cuando se produciría la renovación más amplia de la familia.
Por ahora, no hay confirmación oficial
El dato más importante es que se trata de información no confirmada. NVIDIA y AMD no han anunciado oficialmente que vayan a saltarse 2027 ni han presentado un calendario definitivo para sus próximas arquitecturas.
Tampoco los fabricantes asociados que producen tarjetas gráficas personalizadas tendrían, según estas informaciones, detalles concretos sobre futuros envíos. La ausencia de planes públicos no demuestra que las nuevas GPU vayan a retrasarse hasta 2028, pero coincide con las filtraciones que apuntan a una renovación más lenta del mercado.
PUBLICIDAD
Para los usuarios de PC, el posible retraso llegaría además en un contexto de precios elevados de memoria y otros componentes. Si las nuevas GPU efectivamente se aplazan, NVIDIA y AMD mantendrían durante más tiempo sus actuales generaciones como principales opciones para los jugadores.
Por ahora, habrá que esperar a que ambas compañías presenten oficialmente sus próximos productos para saber si 2027 será realmente un año de transición o si finalmente habrá nuevos lanzamientos antes de 2028.

articles.title: AMD beats Intel to the trillion-dollar club as stock price soars — firm joins Nvidia, Broadcom, and SK hynix for companies worth over $1 trillion
articles.text:
AMD beats Intel to the trillion-dollar club as stock price soars — firm joins Nvidia, Broadcom, and SK hynix for companies worth over $1 trillion
Nvidia first hit $1 trillion in 2023 and has gone onto become the most valuable company in the world.
AMD's market cap has crossed the $1 trillion mark for the first time, following a rally in its share price over the last week. At market close on Friday, AMD's share price was around $557. On Monday morning, shares immediately jumped to $607 on the market open and have continued to rise, finally pushing AMD over the $1 trillion mark.
Saša Marinković, AMD's senior marketing director, shared the milestone on X. Since posting, AMD's share has fluctuated a bit, bringing the market cap down below $1 trillion for brief periods. Undoubtedly, the buzz around the milestone will cause some turmoil in the share price throughout the day, though it should eventually stabilize.
Just a week ago, AMD was quite a ways off hitting the trillion-dollar milestone. AMD's share price has risen by around 29% over the past month, and 21% of that jump came in just the last five days. On Monday alone, AMD's shares jumped around 9% within the first few hours of the market opening.
If you're unfamiliar, market cap is a shorthand for understanding the value of a company. It looks at the number of outstanding shares multiplied by the share price. It's not necessarily tied to revenue or profit, at least not directly. Rather, market cap is a read on the value of a company in the eyes of Wall Street, fluctuating as the share price does.
AMD joins a club of fewer than two dozen companies around the world that have passed a $1 trillion market cap, including SK hynix, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple, Nvidia, Broadcom, and Micron. Although AMD has now joined the club, it's still far behind its rival in the AI accelerator space, Nvidia, which sits at a market cap of around $5.4 trillion currently.
However, AMD was able to beat Intel to the milestone. Intel's market cap currently sits at around $648 billion. Interestingly, Intel has actually seen a larger rally in its share price over the past month. Share prices have risen 37% in the past month, with 25% of that growth coming in the past five days. Similar to AMD, Intel opened on the market Monday morning with a 13% jump.
Following AMD's Q2 earnings, where it beat revenue expectations by 2%, shares traded down, creating an opportunity to hold. That's paying off now as both AMD and Intel shares jump.

articles.title: 409 km d’autonomie réelle en montagne : la Renault 5 réussit son pari le plus difficile
articles.text:
La Lancia Ypsilon qui a battu un record de consommation sur le périphérique parisien vous a bluffé, n’est-ce pas ? Elle a en tout cas fait réagir, avec des sceptiques éparpillés en nombre dans les commentaires. Les conditions n’étaient pas réalistes, dixit certains. Périphérique, bouchons, voiture de série, journée entière… Difficile de faire plus réel, mais passons… Voici le test d’une toute autre nature aussi véritable que le premier.
Le protagoniste est la Renault 5 électrique, qui est passée entre les mains du magazine spécialisé roumain Autocritica. Le test d’autonomie s’est déroulé sur un terrain complètement différent puisque la française a parcouru les 309 km séparant Pitești d’Alba Iulia via l’exigeant massif des Carpates. De quoi faire exploser sa consommation avec un point haut dépassant les 2000 mètres d’altitude. Une catastrophe en perspective ?
12,7 kWh/100 km : une consommation réelle qui fait taire les sceptiques
Pas tant que ça… Pas du tout, même, puisque l’appétit s’est montré particulièrement contenu avec une moyenne réelle de 12,7 kWh/100 km. En se basant sur la batterie Autonomie Confort de 52 kWh, on en tire une autonomie de 409 km, ce qui est extrêmement proche des 410 km revendiqués sur le cycle WLTP. Précisons en plus que le modèle utilisé est une version haut de gamme Roland-Garros plus énergivore.
Le véhicule en question n’était en outre pas encore concerné par la récente mise à jour de la Renault 5 visant à réduire sa consommation. Les dernières versions de la citadine électrique sont désormais capables d’aller jusqu’à 430 km sur une charge. Le test s’est principalement tenu sur routes nationales limitées à 90 km/h ainsi que sur autoroutes bornées comme chez nous à 130 km/h. Le style de conduite ne visait pas l’économie.
L’efficience avant tout : la vraie leçon de ce test
Les conditions météorologiques étaient clémentes avec un temps ensoleillé et un thermomètre oscillant entre 10 et 25°C. Si l’ascension du col a fait grimper la consommation moyenne, c’est la descente qui s’ensuivait qui a permis de revenir illico dans le vert. Le freinage régénératif, encore dépourvu de One Pedal à ce moment-là, s’est montré particulièrement efficace pour remettre de l’énergie dans la batterie.
La performance est remarquable et montre qu’une voiture électrique peut effectivement gambader en confiance en dehors des villes. La nouvelle version de la R5 à l’aérodynamisme retravaillée devrait ainsi faire encore mieux par sa meilleure efficience. Cette dernière est la clé pour augmenter l’autonomie, car agrandir les batteries plus que de raison n’est pas une solution miracle à nos yeux. Qui voudrait des voitures toujours plus lourdes et plus chères ?

articles.title: Tom Cruise y Emily Blunt presentaron en 24 horas y en dos continentes una de las mejores pelis de ciencia ficción de los últimos 15 años
articles.text:
Tom Cruise es conocido por sus hazañas atrevidas y dignas de récord, casi siempre en forma de acrobacias temerarias de esas que quitan el hipo. Pero con 'Al filo del mañana' se sacó de la manga un plan de locos digno de 'Misión Imposible', solo que de otro tipo: tres estrenos, en dos continentes y en apenas 24 horas. Ni uno ni dos: tres, y con el cronómetro en marcha.
La secuela, cada vez más cerca. Una vez más, se han multiplicado los indicios de que pronto arrancará el rodaje de la esperada secuela de 'Edge of Tomorrow', que aquí en España conocemos como 'Al filo del mañana'. Hay que decir que tiene todo el sentido del mundo, porque después del estreno en cines de esta peli de bucles temporales allá por 2014, los fans pedían a gritos una segunda parte.
Un éxito con crítica y taquilla. El filme fue una de esas rarezas que pegan el pelotazo en la taquilla y, al mismo tiempo, dejan tan contento al público como a la prensa especializada. La web estadounidense Rotten Tomatoes recoge un 91% de críticas positivas, mientras que los usuarios también se rinden con un 90% de aprobación. Y el que escribe lo secunda.
Blunt, a ciegas hasta el final. Visto lo visto, cuesta creer que la protagonista, Emily Blunt, se fuera poniendo cada vez más nerviosa según se acercaba el estreno del film de acción y ciencia ficción dirigido por Doug Liman ('Mr. & Mrs. Smith'). Y es que durante mucho tiempo no tuvo ni idea de qué se traía entre manos el equipo de marketing, ni de dónde se iba a proyectar siquiera la película.
Un estreno era poco para Cruise. Lo que ella no sabía es que su compañero de reparto llevaba tiempo con una idea en la cabeza y, como corresponde a la estrella de 'Misión: Imposible' y su afición a las acrobacias, no una cualquiera. No planeaba un estreno, sino tres, en tres ciudades distintas de dos continentes y en 24 horas. "Cuando me enteré de que habría tres estrenos, simplemente dije: 'Esto es una idea de Tom Cruise'", contó la actriz en una entrevista recogida por Sensacine.
Londres, París y Nueva York. Como es imposible celebrar de noche tres estrenos tan alejados entre sí, y con todos los implicados presentes, el maratón arrancó a las 6:30 de la mañana en Londres. Al mediodía llegó el segundo pase en París, antes de que la gira relámpago pusiera su punto final por la noche en Nueva York. ¿Se arrepintió Cruise de su plan descabellado, aunque fuera un poco, después del último vuelo? Por supuesto que no. Y eso que había tomado sus precauciones para que el viaje fuera lo más cómodo posible para el reparto y el equipo.
Un vuelo entero en pijama. En el primer trayecto, Cruise y Blunt coincidieron con el resto del reparto y con el director Doug Liman en el mismo avión, una experiencia que ambos describieron como "muy divertida". El segundo vuelo, el transatlántico, fue algo distinto: esta vez los dos actores viajaron solos en su propio jet, donde pudieron descansar. Según Blunt, ella se pasó toda la travesía en pijama.
"Es como rodar una película". Cruise también echó una cabezada, aunque breve. "Me siento bien, es como rodar una película. Duermes un par de horas, te levantas y sigues", aseguró el hoy actor de 63 años. En el estreno de Nueva York se tomó una hora entera para hacerse fotos con los fans en la alfombra roja.

articles.title: Desarman un iPhone 18 Pro y su interior sorprende: una cámara de vapor gigante y más batería
articles.text:
El iPhone 18 Pro esconde importantes cambios en su interior que no se pueden apreciar a simple vista. Un desmontaje realizado por iFixit revela una cámara de vapor casi tres veces más grande, una batería de mayor capacidad y nuevas soluciones para gestionar el calor generado por el procesador. El equipo también muestra cómo Apple ha conseguido colocar parte del sistema Face ID debajo de la pantalla.
El análisis permite comprobar físicamente algunas de las principales novedades de hardware de los nuevos teléfonos de Apple, aunque también deja en evidencia ciertas dificultades para reparar componentes como la nueva cámara principal con apertura variable.
PUBLICIDAD
Una cámara de vapor mucho más grande
Uno de los cambios más importantes está relacionado con la refrigeración. En el iPhone 18 Pro, Apple modificó la distribución interna para colocar el procesador A20 Pro en la parte exterior de la placa, mientras que la memoria queda desplazada hacia un lateral.
Esta disposición permite que el chip tenga un contacto más directo con el sistema encargado de disipar el calor. Durante el desmontaje, iFixit encontró una esponja térmica que presiona el procesador contra la cámara de vapor.
La diferencia respecto a la generación anterior es considerable. La cámara de vapor ahora ocupa una superficie mucho mayor, cercana a todo el cuerpo del teléfono. Esto permite distribuir el calor generado por el A20 Pro sobre un área más amplia.
PUBLICIDAD
La propia batería también participa en este proceso. Su carcasa metálica ayuda a alejar el calor del procesador y dirigirlo hacia la parte superior del dispositivo, donde puede disiparse a través de la pantalla.
Más batería, especialmente en el Pro Max
El desmontaje también permitió comprobar diferencias en la capacidad de las baterías dependiendo del mercado. iFixit analizó la versión con eSIM que se comercializa en Estados Unidos y otros países.
En este modelo, el iPhone 18 Pro cuenta con una batería de 4.288 mAh, un 0,8 % más que el iPhone 17 Pro. El iPhone 18 Pro Max, en cambio, alcanza los 5.567 mAh, un incremento del 9,4 %.
PUBLICIDAD
En los modelos con bandeja física para tarjetas SIM, las capacidades son diferentes. En España, por ejemplo, el etiquetado energético de la Unión Europea indica 4.056 mAh para el iPhone 18 Pro y 5.391 mAh para el Pro Max. Esto supone aumentos del 1,45 % y 11,8 %, respectivamente, frente a sus antecesores.
Una cámara con piezas extremadamente pequeñas
Otra de las novedades que queda al descubierto es el sistema de apertura variable de la cámara principal. Apple utiliza seis pequeñas láminas que pueden desplazarse para modificar la apertura entre f/1.48 y f/4.0.
Cada una tiene un grosor comparable al de un cabello humano y se mueve mediante un sistema de pequeños electroimanes. El mecanismo funciona de manera independiente al sistema de estabilización óptica de la cámara.
PUBLICIDAD
El desmontaje también muestra una de las consecuencias de este diseño: si el mecanismo de apertura presenta un problema, no existe una reparación sencilla de cada componente. De acuerdo a la evaluación, sería necesario reemplazar el conjunto completo de la cámara.
Face ID también cambia de lugar
Apple ha introducido otra modificación poco visible en el sistema Face ID. La cámara infrarroja utilizada para el reconocimiento facial está situada debajo de la pantalla, mientras que otros elementos del sistema continúan en la Dynamic Island.
iFixit encontró bajo el microscopio una zona de la pantalla donde se ha eliminado una fila de píxeles de cada dos justo encima del sensor. El patrón se difumina progresivamente hacia los bordes para hacerlo prácticamente imperceptible.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, debajo del panel OLED hay un filtro que permite pasar la luz infrarroja y bloquea la luz visible. De esta manera, el sensor puede funcionar sin que el área modificada resulte evidente para el usuario.
El módem depende del mercado
El desmontaje también encontró una diferencia entre modelos. Todos los iPhone 18 Pro y Pro Max incorporan el módem C2 desarrollado por Apple, excepto el iPhone 18 Pro Max vendido en Estados Unidos, que mantiene un módem de Qualcomm.
Una posible explicación está relacionada con los acuerdos previos entre Apple y Qualcomm. El chip de Qualcomm tendría además un consumo energético superior al C2, por lo que su presencia en el modelo estadounidense podría estar vinculada a la batería de mayor capacidad del Pro Max.
PUBLICIDAD
En conjunto, el desmontaje muestra que buena parte de las novedades del iPhone 18 Pro están precisamente donde el usuario no puede verlas: en la gestión del calor, la batería, las cámaras, el reconocimiento facial y la conectividad.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Últimas horas: Galaxy A37 (256 GB) tem queda agressiva de 55% com cupom • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Últimas horas: Galaxy A37 (256 GB) tem queda agressiva de 55% com cupom
Galaxy A37 de 256 GB traz tela AMOLED de 120 Hz, bateria de 5.000 mAh e 8 GB de RAM. Celular está em promoção no Mercado Livre ao combinar Pix e cupom válido por mais poucas horas
O Galaxy A37 (256 GB) está em promoção no Mercado Livre por R$ 1.618 no Pix com o cupom MELIACHAHOJE. O valor representa um desconto significativo de 55% sobre o preço original de R$ 3.599, mas que dura apenas por mais algumas horas ou até o cupom esgotar.
O smartphone da Samsung lançado em abril promete repetir a proposta da geração passada com acesso a inteligência artificial a um custo mais baixo.
Galaxy A37 leva tela AMOLED de 120 Hz e bateria de 5.000 mAh
O painel Super AMOLED de 6,7 polegadas entrega resolução Full HD+ e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz, possibilitando rolagens, jogos e animações gráficas fluidas. Além disso, o componente conta com a proteção Gorilla Glass Victus+ e atinge brilho de 1.900 nits, um nível que permite a visualização sob alta luminosidade.
Para tirar fotografias, o dispositivo possui três câmeras traseiras. O destaque vai para a principal de 50 MP, a mesma utilizada no A57, que entrega bons resultados pelo menos para fotos diurnas. O conjunto também inclui uma ultrawide de 8 MP e macro de 5 MP. Enquanto a frontal de 12 MP realiza gravações de vídeos em 4K.
De acordo com a Samsung, a bateria de 5.000 mAh do Galaxy A37 sustenta até 29 horas para reprodução de vídeos. Logo, proporciona autonomia com folga para um dia de uso típico com redes sociais e outros apps. Outro ponto positivo é o suporte a carregamento rápido de até 45 W, mas que precisa ser adquirido separadamente.
O celular intermediário deixou de utilizar processador Snapdragon (equipado no A36) e agora usa o Exynos 1480 de 4 nanômetros com CPU octa-core de 2.75 GHz. Além disso, acompanha 8 GB de RAM e 256 GB de armazenamento. A configuração proporciona desempenho satisfatório e sem engasgos para tarefas com exigência média.
Lançado com o Android 16 e One UI 8.5, o A37 disponibiliza ferramentas apoiadas por inteligência artificial. A suíte Galaxy AI conta com funcionalidades para otimização de pesquisas, tarefas relacionadas a edições de imagens, edições inteligentes de imagens e etc. A Samsung garante até seis anos de novas atualizações de software.
O Galaxy A37 (256 GB) à venda por R$ 1.618 no Pix com o cupom MELIACHAHOJE ainda possui certificação IP68, no qual fornece forte proteção contra poeira e água. Adquira-o já antes que o cupom acabe!

articles.title: AMD Ryzen 5 5500F and 7500 show up at retail with pricing above MSRP — budget CPUs are $20 more expensive than list price, even from first-party sellers
articles.text:
AMD Ryzen 5 5500F and 7500 show up at retail with pricing above MSRP — budget CPUs are $20 more expensive than list price, even from first-party sellers
Hopefully additional retailer listings will bring prices back down to MSRP.
AMD's new Ryzen 5 5500F and Ryzen 5 7500 are available for sale, though the prices are higher than AMD originally suggested. On Amazon, the Ryzen 5 5500F is available for $120, while the Ryzen 5 7500 is listed at $210, both $20 more expensive than AMD's suggested retail pricing. Both are sold directly by Amazon, suggesting we'll see slightly higher prices for these two chips than AMD originally suggested.
AMD revealed the budget CPUs nearly two weeks ago, and despite launching on that date, the chips haven't been available for sale in the U.S. until now. The Ryzen 5 5500F is particularly interesting, as the $90 Ryzen 5 5500 has continually been among Amazon's best sellers in CPUs. Although the Ryzen 5 5500 and 5500F sound similar, there are actually quite a few differences between the two CPUs.
Both are six-core, 12-thread chips using AMD's Zen 3 architecture, but the 5500 falls under the Cezanne family, while the 5500F falls under Vermeer. The 5500F comes with PCIe 4, compared to PCIe 3 on the 5500, as well as a higher 4.4 GHz boost clock — the base 5500 tops out at 4.2 GHz. These changes apparently allow the 5500F to achieve higher performance, somewhere in the range of 5% to 10%, in games. We'll be getting the CPU in the Tom's Hardware lab to test the performance ourselves.
Although Zen 3 is aging, it has become an ideal home for budget builders as the RAM pricing crisis continues to surge. In addition to the Ryzen 5 5500F, we saw AMD re-release the Ryzen 7 5800X3D earlier this year to combat rising DDR5 prices.
We took the Ryzen 5 5500 (non-F) out for a spin earlier this year for a budget $100 CPU shootout. Generally, it underperforms the Intel competition at this price, but a 5% to 10% jump would close that gap. If performance holds up, the Ryzen 5 5500F may have a shot at our best CPUs for gaming list with its low price.
The Ryzen 5 7500 is easier to parse. It's identical to the 7500F, just with integrated graphics. It comes with six Zen 4 cores for a total of 12 threads, and unlike the 5500, it exclusively supports DDR5 memory. The 7500 comes with a boost clock of 5 GHz and supports PCIe 5. Like the 5500F, it has a 65W TDP and comes bundled with AMD's Wraith Stealth cooler.
AMD originally announced the Ryzen 5 5500F at $99 and the 7500 at $190, though the current Amazon listings are both $20 higher than that — $120 and $210, respectively. At the time of writing, the CPUs are only available at Amazon in the U.S.; Micro Center and Newegg don't have listings available. When other retailers pick up the chips, prices could come down.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
This isn't the first time we've seen oddly high prices on new AMD releases at Amazon. Earlier this year, the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 went up for sale on Amazon prior to release, selling for $1,000, $100 above MSRP. After the launch dust settled and listings went up at other retailers, the pricing dropped back down to $900. Hopefully, we'll see something similar happen here.

articles.title: 'It was exhausting to film' — Outlander: Blood of my Blood season 2 star opens up about shooting 'unsettling' episode 1 time-travel scene
articles.text:
Outlander: Blood of my Blood season 2 episode 1 star on 'unsettling' opening scene that you won't have seen coming — 'it was exhausting to film'
Outlander meets American Horror Story
Spoilers for Outlander: Blood of my Blood season 2 episode 1 ahead.
Outlander: Blood of my Blood season 2 has officially kicked off on Starz (US) and MGM+ (international)... and boy, is it off to an explosive start.
Alongside some great Easter eggs (IYKYK), we've picked the action back up with Claire and Jamie's parents: Brian (Jamie Roy), Ellen (Harriet Slater), Julia (Hermione Corfield), and Henry (Jeremy Irvine).
The lovers are separated once again as the Scottish Highlands are split in two by the 1715 Jacobite Rising in season 2, with Julia and Henry split when their plan to travel back to the 1920s goes wrong at the last minute.
It was brutal, but somehow Henry has found himself in a psychiatric asylum in 1924, while Julia stays trapped in 1715... with no idea what's happened or how to fix it.
We see Henry undergo electric shock therapy after it's revealed that he was found on the street by a local policeman, incoherently babbling about time travel enough to cause concern.
It's a brutal scene to watch, but how was it to film? Irvine gives us a full breakdown... and it might actually have been worse than it looked.
'It really jumps in at the deep end'
"It's great. I got to do a load of research into something that I didn't know much about," Irvine tells me. "I'd watched some footage of people having it done, and that was a good excuse to sort of really jump in at the deep end... go for quite a big performance and um, see if we got away with it."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
If you ask me, it certainly does. As I tell Irvine, season 2 episode 1 largely feels less like Outlander and more like an episode of American Horror Story or Ratched. For the tonal shift alone, I'm hooked — there's nothing like keeping us on our toes right from the get-go.
"I remember it being exhausting to film," he continues. I think I basically had a seizure for two days on a gurney. I really enjoyed the wacky way they went inside Henry's mind. I think that it's the part of the character that I enjoy playing the most, his fragile mental state and his warped view on reality.
"It's a great obstacle for him to have to try and work through. It's unsettling for me to watch back, which I think is a good, good thing."
If you've been following my Blood of my Blood coverage since season 1, you might remember that Irvine told me shortly after starting production that season 2 would be "wildly not what we expect." But now that we're all seeing it, were the actors as surprised when the drama picked back up?
"I remember before I read the scripts, I went for a costume fitting and had a vicar's outfit and a straitjacket to try on... that's when my suspicions were first aroused," Irvine adds. "For Henry, it's a completely different world to go into, which is great.
"We filmed episode 1 in that first month, which was nice because you don't always get to film in order. It was great to see how everybody just came back and hit the ground running pretty much from that first step."
But if you think this means that things are slowly down from episode 2 onwards, think again.

articles.title: Il tient deux jours loin d'une prise : le Redmi Note 15 Pro+ 5G 12+512 Go est à 371,32€
articles.text:
Xiaomi place son Redmi Note 15 Pro+ 5G face à des flagships trois fois plus chers, avec un écran de 6,83 pouces et une batterie de 6 500 mAh. Reste à savoir ce que la configuration 12+512 Go concède réellement pour tenir ce tarif.
Le Redmi Note 15 Pro+ 5G occupe le haut de la série lancée par Xiaomi pour la rentrée 2026. Il embarque un écran AMOLED CrystalRes de 6,83 pouces à 120 Hz, une puce Snapdragon 7s Gen 4, une batterie de 6 500 mAh compatible charge 100 W et une certification IP66/IP68/IP69K. Vous trouverez le Redmi Note 15 Pro+ 5G 12+512 Go à 371,32 € chez AliExpress, quand la Fnac affiche cette même configuration 549 €. Le public concerné est celui qui regarde du côté des flagships Android sans vouloir y engager le budget correspondant.
Le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro+ 5G en 12+512 Go est affiché à 371,32 € au lieu de 402,98 € sur AliExpress.
Pourquoi choisir le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro+ 5G ?
- Une autonomie qui tient deux jours : Le labo de la Fnac a mesuré 18 h 33 d’usage continu, contre 11 h 01 pour la génération précédente. Vous partez le matin sans câble et vous rentrez le lendemain soir avec de la marge.
- Un écran lisible en plein soleil : La dalle AMOLED 1,5K monte à 3 200 nits en pic. De quoi rester lisible en terrasse au mois d’août, là où un écran moyen décroche.
- 512 Go sans rationner la mémoire : Vous gardez plusieurs années de photos et une bibliothèque de jeux installée, quand un Pixel 11 Pro à 1 199 € s’arrête à 256 Go sur son premier palier.
Un smartphone de contenu avant d’être un smartphone photo
Le format de 6,83 pouces et la luminosité de la dalle orientent l’usage vers la consommation de contenu. Une série regardée dans le train ou un match suivi en terrasse profitent directement de cette surface et de ce pic à 3 200 nits. La puce Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 fait tourner les jeux 3D exigeants à 60 images par seconde, ce qui couvre confortablement les usages du quotidien. La technologie Wet Touch permet en prime de garder la main sur l’écran avec les doigts mouillés.
Ce profil parle surtout aux gros consommateurs de vidéo et aux joueurs occasionnels qui veulent éviter la recharge de milieu de journée. Il convient moins bien à qui cherche un téléphone maniable : plus de 200 grammes et plus de 16 centimètres de hauteur, cela se sent dans une poche. Les photographes réguliers sont l’autre public mal servi, malgré le capteur de 200 mégapixels mis en avant sur la fiche produit.
Face à un Pixel 11 Pro ou à un Galaxy S26 Ultra, où passe l’écart de prix ?
L’écart avec un flagship se paye sur deux postes précis, la photo et le suivi logiciel. Le capteur de 200 mégapixels délivre des images correctes en plein jour, mais sature les couleurs et décroche en basse lumière, là où un Pixel joue sa réputation. Le suivi s’arrête pour sa part à quatre mises à jour majeures, à partir d’un Android 15 déjà daté au lancement. Notre comparatif des meilleurs smartphones place le Galaxy S26 Ultra en tête du classement Android, et ce n’est pas pour son tarif.
✅ Les points forts
- Autonomie mesurée à 18 h 33, soit deux journées d’usage courant
- Écran AMOLED 1,5K de 6,83 pouces à 120 Hz, jusqu’à 3 200 nits
- Charge 100 W, batterie remplie en 47 minutes
- 12 Go de mémoire vive et 512 Go de stockage
- Certification IP66/IP68/IP69K
❌ Les limites
- Photo correcte de jour, en retrait sur la colorimétrie et en basse lumière
- Android 15 au lancement, quatre mises à jour majeures annoncées
- Interface HyperOS livrée avec de la publicité à désactiver
- Pas de charge sans fil, vidéo plafonnée en 4K à 30 i/s
La remise immédiate reste modeste, 371,32 € au lieu de 402,98 € : c’est face aux 549 € de la Fnac que l’offre AliExpress prend tout son sens.
Le Redmi Note 15 Pro+ 5G ne remplace pas un flagship et ne prétend pas le faire. Il en reprend en revanche les deux postes les plus visibles au quotidien, l’écran et l’autonomie, et il les tient sérieusement. À 371,32 € pour la configuration 12+512 Go, il place l’économie là où elle se voit le moins, dans le traitement photo et dans la durée du suivi logiciel.
Si vous hésitiez à engager 1 199 € dans un Pixel 11 Pro pour regarder des vidéos, jouer un peu et finir la journée avec de la batterie, l’arbitrage penche nettement de ce côté. Si vous photographiez souvent, en intérieur ou de nuit, l’écart se creuse dans l’autre sens et l’économie devient un vrai renoncement. articles.title: 1 100 km d’autonomie à 45 000 € : BYD lance la voiture électrique « la plus endurante au monde »
articles.text:
En matière de véhicule électrique, les Chinois en connaissent un rayon. C’est du moins ce que l’on est tenté de se dire vu les dernières annonces de BYD. Sa marque haut de gamme Denza lance en effet la berline Z9S sur le marché local. Sa particularité ? Être la voiture électrique avec la plus grande autonomie au monde, dixit le constructeur. Avec 1 100 km mesurés dans sa version de pointe, on semble effectivement y être…
Et son tarif n’a absolument rien d’extravagant, puisqu’il est fixé à 349 800 yuans, soit environ 45 000 € au taux de change actuel. Une électrique de 5,09 mètres avec 1 100 km d’autonomie à ce prix-là ? Mais où va l’Europe ? Vers des chiffres s’approchant davantage du réel, peut-être ? Car les 1 100 km d’autonomie de la Denza ont été mesurés sur le cycle CLTC chinois, bien arrangeant pour les constructeurs.
À lire aussi : 960 km d’autonomie et recharge en 5 min – ce SUV de rêve qu’on ne verra probablement jamais
Promesse chinoise vs réalité européenne : à quoi s’attendre vraiment ?
Cela ferait alors à peu près 850 km sur notre norme WLTP. La Z9S perd alors son titre autoproclamé face aux Mercedes EQS et Lucid Air dépassant toutes deux la barre des 900 km en WLTP. Qu’importe, la performance reste impressionnante rapportée au prix car la chinoise est au bas mot trois fois moins chère que les rivales précitées. Et il reste en plus un domaine dans lequel la Denza surpasse réellement la Mercedes et la Lucid.
Il s’agit de la recharge rapide, où la batterie Blade 2.0 de 122,496 kWh ne fait qu’une bouchée des deux occidentales. Avec une puissance maximale de 1 500 kW en courant continu DC, la Z9S passe de 10 à 70 % de charge en 5 minutes et de 10 à 97 % en seulement 9 minutes. C’est ce coup-ci vraiment un record mondial rendu possible par les bornes ultra-rapides Flash Charger bien présentes en Chine et en cours de déploiement en Europe.
Un arsenal technologique digne d’une berline du futur
Bien sûr, il existe des variantes moins endurantes au catalogue avec 102,326 kWh et 920 km d’autonomie CLTC. Et plus puissantes, aussi : trois machines électriques et 1 193 ch, pour tracer efficacement à travers le pays. Dans tous les cas, la Z9S est un véhicule résolument premium avec son intérieur couvert de cuir Nappa et de daim. La liste d’équipements est longue comme un lundi matin.
Le LiDAR intégré au toit alimente par exemple le logiciel God’s Eye B permettant la conduite entièrement autonome du début à la fin. Les roues arrière directrices réduisent le rayon de braquage à peau de chagrin alors que la suspension pneumatique à double chambre DiSus-A isole complètement des irrégularités de la route. Un sacré véhicule vendu à un prix insolent qui n’est bien entendu pas pour nous…
