articles.title: AMD just joined the $1 trillion club, beating Intel to the milestone
articles.text:
In a nutshell: AMD has become only the fourth US chipmaker to reach a $1 trillion valuation, following in the footsteps of Broadcom, Micron, and Nvidia. AMD's stock entered 2026 at a price of $223.47 and would dip below the $200 mark a few times before climbing in April. As of writing, shares are trading at $607.24 – a healthy return for anyone that bought in early this year.
Nvidia eclipsed the $1 trillion valuation mark in May 2023, and has not looked back since. The company has continued to tack on value driven largely by the AI boom. Currently, the chipmaker has an incredible market cap of roughly $5.48 trillion, making it the most valuable company in the world by a sizable margin.
Apple, for comparison, is worth around $4.94 trillion. Google ranks third with a market cap of $4.29 trillion. Microsoft, another major player in the tech space, is worth $3.69 trillion as of today.
Credit: App Economy Insights
AMD is not the only chipmaker to start the week strong. Shares in Intel are trading up more than 12% on the day, and Qualcomm's stock is up nearly 8.3%. Broadcom is having a slower day, up just 1.22% as of this writing.
Intel, often considered AMD's primary rival due to their long history in the CPU industry, is also having a stellar 2026. Share values are up 208% year to date, but the company's market cap sits at just $643.5 billion – far behind AMD's.
Last month, AMD CEO Lisa Su said the company expects to double data center sales in 2027. That was welcome news considering the stock's dip in July and August.
Like others, AMD is benefiting from the ongoing AI boom. At some point, however, the demand for AI hardware will cool. Fortunately for AMD, the company has other divisions to lean on when the time comes. For others that are putting all of their eggs in the AI basket, the outcome could be far more catastrophic.

articles.title: Trump rejects AI slowdown calls, launches "AI Force" instead
articles.text:
Donald Trump has said that the US would appoint a new AI tsar and create an “AI Force” while offering a full-throated defense of the emerging industry in the face of a growing popular backlash.
The US president’s announcement comes as leading industry figures have sounded the alarm that humans could lose control over the rapidly advancing technology without a slowdown in development.
However, rather than announcing regulation as some have demanded, Trump has dismissed safety concerns as a “hoax.”
“I will be announcing, in the near future, the AI “Tsar” —Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!” Posted Trump on his social media platform Truth Social.
“AI is the next Industrial Revolution, or Internet, but will be even larger and more impactful, possibly as much as 25% of our Country’s GDP. We are leading China, and the rest of the World, and I intend to keep it that way!”
Trump said that the backlash to AI and the proliferation of data centers to power it was one of a series of “hoaxes” created by the Left, along with “Russiagate,” climate change, and “Transgender for Everyone.”
“It all began with an attack on our Data Centers, until people realized how wealthy and prestigious they were for the Communities in which they were built,” Trump said in the Truth post.
“We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry. Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows!”

articles.title: MediaTek Dimensity CX C10 Max Offers Flagship Performance to a New Era of AI-First Laptops
articles.text:
Monday, September 21st 2026
	
	
	
	
MediaTek Dimensity CX C10 Max Offers Flagship Performance to a New Era of AI-First Laptops
MediaTek, a global leader in computing and mobile technologies, today introduced the MediaTek Dimensity CX C10 Max, the inaugural SoC for the company's new Dimensity Compute Experiences (CX) family. As the flagship of the lineup, Dimensity CX C10 Max combines exceptional performance, advanced functionality, and impressive power efficiency to enable an upcoming premium, ultra-portable Googlebook device.
Built on TSMC's advanced 3 nm process, Dimensity CX C10 Max utilizes an All Big Core design with octa-core CPU, 11-core GPU, and MediaTek's 8th-generation NPU in a highly efficient platform engineered to deliver stellar performance across multitasking, productivity, entertainment, intelligent assistance, and more. Its power-efficient architecture enables manufacturers to design thinner, lighter, and fanless devices with all-day battery life.The MediaTek NPU 890 delivers up to 55 TOPS of performance, helping enable upcoming Googlebook devices to better deliver an experience that's a step ahead. Further expanding MediaTek's AI leadership spanning from the Edge to the cloud, MediaTek NPU 890 is designed to power Gemini Intelligence features, delivering faster responses and offering additional privacy benefits.
"Dimensity CX C10 Max is designed for the next wave of intelligent computing, combining flagship performance and power-efficient processing to ensure an incredible user experience paired with amazing battery life," said Vince Hu, Senior Vice President & General Manager of Data Center & Computing Business at MediaTek. "Bringing these capabilities to Googlebook builds on our leadership in Android computing and continues our long history of collaboration with Google."
The MediaTek Imagiq 1090 ISP integrated into the Dimensity CX C10 Max delivers best-in-class professional camera quality. Supporting camera sensors of up to 32MP, the AI-ISP enables high-quality HDR video capture, smooth video zoom, cinematic video, and sustained focus; resulting in clearer, more immersive video calls, livestreams and content creation.
The platform also supports Wi-Fi 7 connectivity with speeds of up to 7.3 Gbps, providing fast, reliable connections for streaming, downloads, and video conferencing in busy wireless environments. Dual-engine Bluetooth 6.0 support provides efficient connectivity for wireless peripherals and audio devices.
By bringing together All Big Core CPU, powerful GPU and MediaTek's industry-leading NPU with accelerated agentic AI, Dimensity CX C10 Max is designed to crunch through the most demanding tasks and deliver ultra-fast multitasking to achieve maximum productivity.

"Dimensity CX C10 Max is designed for the next wave of intelligent computing, combining flagship performance and power-efficient processing to ensure an incredible user experience paired with amazing battery life," said Vince Hu, Senior Vice President & General Manager of Data Center & Computing Business at MediaTek. The MediaTek Imagiq 1090 ISP integrated into the Dimensity CX C10 Max delivers best-in-class professional camera quality. The platform also supports Wi-Fi 7 connectivity with speeds of up to 7.3 Gbps, providing fast, reliable connections for streaming, downloads, and video conferencing in busy wireless environments. Dual-engine Bluetooth 6.0 support provides efficient connectivity for wireless peripherals and audio devices.
By bringing together All Big Core CPU, powerful GPU and MediaTek's industry-leading NPU with accelerated agentic AI, Dimensity CX C10 Max is designed to crunch through the most demanding tasks and deliver ultra-fast multitasking to achieve maximum productivity.

articles.title: 'Success is not guaranteed, but excitement is' — Tesla wants your money for the Roadster it hasn’t unveiled yet
articles.text:
Tesla is taking $50k deposits for its next-gen Roadster that nobody's even seen yet — so here's your reminder that it never actually produced the last Roadster it took $50k deposits for
Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me
- Tesla has re-opened the order books for its long-awaited Roadster
- It is asking buyers for a $50,000 deposit
- Some customers have been waiting since 2017 for news of their cars
Tesla has announced that it will finally reveal the next generation Roadster in October during a glitzy event in Waco, Texas... although we still really don’t know what to expect.
Reports suggest the high-performance EV could use cold-gas thrusters, developed by SpaceX, to produce previously unseen levels of acceleration, while others have stated that the car itself has received a 'Cyber' redesign since the 2017 car was first unveiled.
What we do know is that Tesla wants your money. It has re-opened the reservations list to be among the first allocated build slots of the electric sports car when (or if) it eventually goes on sale.
Similarly to the 2017 launch, the EV company is asking for a $5,000 “fully-refundable” instant credit or debit card payment, followed by a $45,000 wire transfer due within 10 days to reserve a build slot.
While we are still firmly left in the dark about the final cost of the upcoming Roadster, it was previously stated that customers would have to hand over a further $250,000 for a “Founders Series” vehicle, which was initially claimed to have been promised for the year 2020.
Back then, Tesla customers were backing a promise of a 600+ mile electric range, a sub-2 second 0-60mph sprint time and a top speed in excess of 250mph.
Fast-forward nine years and the speculation has been blown up to sci-fi proportions, but more importantly, all of those original customers are yet to receive a new vehicle.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Tesla CEO Elon Musk has stated that the October demonstration will be a “banger” and that the company needed to invite an audience to “vouch for the fact that this is not AI,” but those who placed deposits are likely just hoping a real vehicle arrives on stage.
Analysis: all speculation?
We can spend hours theorizing about what we might see during Tesla’s October Roadster event, whether that’s a vehicle that hovers for a brief time or the use of banned F1 aero tech that creates massive amounts of downforce... it’s all up for discussion.
Alas, it’s worth noting that Tesla hasn’t launched an all-new model since the Cybertruck, which wasn’t exactly the success story that the company had hoped. In fact, sales of that model have been in steep decline since its initial reveal in 2023.
The Cybertruck program also proved that it pays to take Tesla’s facts with a pinch of salt, as everything from its off-road abilities, electric range, build quality and even price have been brought into question during its lifetime.
October 1 will hopefully reveal all. But those queuing to place a deposit should proceed with caution.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Leon has been navigating a world where automotive and tech collide for almost 20 years, reporting on everything from in-car entertainment to robotised manufacturing plants. Currently, EVs are the focus of his attentions, but give it a few years and it will be electric vertical take-off and landing craft. Outside of work hours, he can be found tinkering with distinctly analogue motorcycles, because electric motors are no replacement for an old Honda inline four.

articles.title: Apple Mac mini (Late 2026) Review: Strong performance, but losing its grip on value
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
Apple’s latest mini machine delivers the generational performance improvements we expect, dampened by the realities of AI price hikes.
Pros
- +Strong single- and multi-threaded performance
- +Storage performance improvements over previous M4 model
- +Small footprint
Cons
- -Recent price hikes erode the Mac mini’s value proposition
- -Memory and storage upgrades are now even pricier
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
It’s been nearly two years since Apple updated the Mac mini. And for better or worse, things have changed a lot during that time. The last Mac mini with an M4 processor went on sale in early November 2024, with a starting price of $599. The latest Mac mini that we’re testing today starts at $899, which we can directly blame on the rising costs of components due to the voracious demand for everything related to artificial intelligence (AI).
A $300 price hike in less than two years is unprecedented, but it’s a sign of the times, and we have to factor those realities when evaluating any product today. So with that context in mind, we’ll take a look at Apple’s newest Mac mini, which looks very familiar on the outside, but has undergone some internal hardware upgrades, to deliver some significant performance improvements over its predecessor.
Design of the Apple Mac mini (M6)
The Mac mini hasn’t changed on the design front, and that’s mostly a good thing. I’m always impressed with not only the minimalist style of this small form-factor computer, but also its tiny size. It has a 5-inch x 5-inch footprint, while standing just 2 inches tall. My only gripe is the power button, which remains stubbornly on the bottom of the system (back left corner). You’ll need to lift the system any time you want to turn it on (or force it to shut down in the event of a crash), and you’ll need to double-tap the power button when setting up Touch ID with an Apple Magic Keyboard for the first time. However, this is just a minor annoyance, as interacting with the power button on a modern Mac is a rarity.
Despite its trim dimensions, you do get a fairly decent number of ports on the exterior of the Mac mini. However, let’s get this out of the way first: Apple doesn’t give you any USB-A ports on the Mac mini, so keep that in mind before purchasing. So, if you have USB-A devices around, you’ll either need to keep some cheap USB-A to USB-C adapters on hand, or invest in a USB-C or Thunderbolt dock for connecting legacy devices.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Instead, our Mac mini review unit features two USB-C ports (10 Gbps) and a 3.5 mm headphone jack up front, along with three Thunderbolt 4 ports on the rear (M5 Pro systems swap the Thunderbolt 4 ports for Thunderbolt 5). You’ll also find a 2.5 GbE port (up from 1 GbE), an HDMI port, and the power port on the back. We should note that while our review unit was specced with the 2.5 GbE LAN, you can individually option a 10 GbE port for $100 extra. A 10 GbE USB-C adapter would set you back around $100, so Apple’s upgrade is surprisingly reasonably priced, and you don’t lose a port in the process.
When it comes to wireless connectivity, the Mac mini uses Apple’s new in-house N1 wireless chip instead of relying on a third-party design. It provides tri-band Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support, which is an upgrade from the Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 on the previous generation.
One thing to keep in mind with the Mac mini is that what you see is what you get when you purchase one. There are no internal upgrades available for the system once you’ve purchased it, so choose wisely before you click the buy button. Base systems come with an M6 chip (12-core CPU, 12-core GPU), 16GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD. Our review unit features the M6 chip, 24GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD. If you want to add storage post-purchase, we’d suggest taking a look at one of the best external SSDs.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Apple Mac mini (M6) Specifications
| Processor | Apple M6 (2 super cores, 4 performance cores, 6 efficiency cores) | 
| Graphics | 12-core GPU | 
| Memory | 24GB LPDDR5X unified memory | 
| Storage | 512GB SSD | 
| Networking | 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 | 
| Front Ports | 2x USB Type-C (10GB/s), 3.5 mm headphone jack | 
| Rear Ports | 3x Thunderbolt 4 ports (USB-C), HDMI, Ethernet | 
| Power Supply | Internal, 155W | 
| Operating System | macOS 27 Golden Gate | 
| Dimensions | 5 x 5 x 2 inches | 
| Price as Configured | $1,399 | 
Productivity Performance on the Apple Mac mini (M6)
Although the Mac mini is available with a more potent M5 Pro processor, our review unit came with the base M6 processor (12 CPU cores, 12 GPU cores). It also incorporates 24GB of LPDDR5X memory and a 512GB SSD.
This is the first system we’ve tested with the new 2-nanometer M6 processor. So, we were eager to see how it would perform against not only the M4 Pro in the previous Mac mini, but also the M5, which can be found in the current-generation MacBook Air and base MacBook Pro.
The M6 chip in the Mac mini had no trouble dispatching the M4, M4 Pro, and M5-equipped systems in the Geekbench synthetic CPU benchmark. In fact, it was 21 percent faster than the last M4 Pro Mac Mini in the single-core test. It also completely obliterated the M4 (10-core CPU, 10-core GPU) version of the Mac mini. The advantage versus the M5 system was lessened, but it was still a clear victory for the M6. The M6 actually slightly trailed the M4 Pro Mac mini (21,045 versus 22,661) in the multi-core test, which wasn’t too surprising given that the 12-core M6 was going up against a 16-core M4 Pro. But it was still a strong showing for the M6, given the architectural improvements that allowed it to get that close.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
We had some trouble obtaining consistent performance from our usual 25GB file transfer test, so we fell back to the Blackmagic Disk Speed Test for benchmarking the 512GB SSD. Needless to say, it presented a marked improvement over the preceding M4 Mac mini.
Storage performance was comparable to the M5 MacBook Pro on sequential writes, but slightly behind for sequential reads. It also slightly outperformed the M4 Pro Mac mini in writes, but was over 1,000 MBps ahead in reads. However, the M6 Mac Mini nearly doubled the write performance and more than doubled the read performance of the M4 Mac mini.
The similar multi-core performance in Geekbench was mirrored in our HandBrake test, during which we transcoded a 4K video file to 1080p. The M6 Mac mini completed the task in 2 minutes and 46 seconds, while the M4 Pro version was just one second behind. The M6 Mac mini was nearly 2 minutes faster than its M4 counterpart.
We ran Cinebench 2026 through 10 runs with the Mac mini, keeping track of its scores along the way. The Mac mini started off with a score of 5403, which rose to 5557 for the second run. For the remaining eight runs, the Mac mini was highly consistent, hovering between 5530 and 5554.
The M6 used in the Mac mini isn't yet fully supported by TG Pro, so we could only use the average of the available temperature sensors (power management sensors, power supply, and SSD). At idle, the fan spun at just around 1,000 revolutions per minute (RPM), with an average system temperature of 44 degrees Celsius. However, when running Cinebench 2026, the average system temperature rose to 64 degrees C, while the fan settled at around 2615 RPM.
Gaming and Graphics on the Apple Mac mini (M6)
Gaming shouldn’t be the primary goal with the Mac mini, but it can do some light lifting. I played Cyberpunk 2077 for a bit and benchmarked it. Although I was provided an Apple Studio Display (5K resolution) to test with the Mac mini, I ran benchmarks at 2560 x 1440 and 1920 x 1080, because the native 5K is a bridge too far for this game, given the hardware.
Using the "For this Mac" global setting, the Mac mini achieved 37.33 frames per second (fps) at 1440p and 58.11 fps at 1080p. With frame generation turned on, those numbers jumped to 62.61 fps and 96.24 fps, respectively.
If you don't mind turning the detail settings down a bit, you can achieve playable frame rates with the Mac mini. However, moving the detail slider to Ray Tracing (Medium) dropped frame rates into the 20 fps range even with frame generation turned on at 1440p.
macOS Golden Gate and Apple Intelligence
The Mac mini ships with macOS 27 Golden Gate, which was first made available to the public last week. macOS 27 is not a complete rethink of the desktop operating system formula for Apple, but it does provide a number of quality-of-life improvements for users.
One of the headlining features is new and improved Siri AI. While Siri was one of the first digital assistants to debut on a smartphone, it hasn't exactly been "smart," at least compared to its contemporaries. Siri AI now digs its fingers deeper into the operating system, allowing it to glean contextual data from your photos, mail, messages, and documents. You can access Siri AI from Spotlight (search) or using the dedicated Siri AI app. Siri AI is also vastly more useful, as it will more consistently answer general questions asked, rather than throw up its digital hands and say "Here's what I found on the web."
Apple's Shortcuts app is an incredibly powerful tool that has been available for years across the Mac, iPhone, and iPad product families. However, the granular control and seemingly limitless options can make creating a new shortcut daunting for newbies. So with macOS 27, you can now create a new Shortcut using natural language. For example, you could input, "Create a shortcut that sets the AC to 74 degrees when I leave work, and let my wife know what time I'll arrive at home," and it will take care of the rest.
Liquid Glass was one of the more controversial additions to macOS 26, with some people not liking the translucent makeover. MacOS 27 gives users more control over Liquid Glass, with sliders to adjust the intensity of the transparency effect.
Apple has also introduced plenty of system-level optimizations to improve performance across the board. For example, Apple says that AirDrop is up to 80 percent faster in macOS 27 than macOS 26, and a lot more reliable. Apps also open faster – any lagginess or stuttering that was perceptible in macOS 26 has been eliminated with this newest release. The best comparison I can make for the macOS 26 to macOS 27 upgrade is the fine-tuning that Apple did going from Mac OS X 10.5 Leopard to Mac OS X 10.6 Snow Leopard. There weren’t any major feature additions with that latter release, but there were a plethora of under-the-hood optimizations that made it much faster and more stable.
In addition, macOS 27 doesn’t install the Rosetta x86 translation software by default; you’ll need to download it when you first run a legacy x86 app. However, starting next year with macOS 28, you won’t be able to run apps that aren’t Apple Silicon-native, so Rosetta will be completely off the table.
Apple Mac mini (M6) Configurations and Warranty
The base Mac Mini comes with an M6 processor, 16GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD for $899. Before Apple's June 2026 price increases, the base Mac mini with M4, 16GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD cost $599. After the price increases, that $599 jumped to $799. Now, we're looking at another $100 increase for the base Mac Mini. There’s one standalone upgrade option: $100 extra gets you a 10 GbE port instead of the standard 2.5 GbE.
Apple also allows you to upgrade to 24GB or 32GB of RAM, along with 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB SSD options. A fully-loaded M6 Mac mini with 32GB of RAM, a 2TB SSD, and 10 GbE costs $2,399.
For people who require a bit more processing power, perhaps for AI tasks (as Apple seems so inclined to believe), the base M5 Pro Mac Mini (15-core CPU, 16-core GPU), with 24GB of RAM and a 512GB SSD, costs $1,699. However, you can go bonkers with the options, topping out with an M5 Pro (18-core CPU, 20-core GPU), 64GB of RAM, an 8TB SSD, and a 10 GbE adapter for a whopping $6,599. At that price, it’s probably worth looking at the Mac Studio.
All Mac minis come with a 1-year manufacturer warranty.
Bottom Line
The base M6 chip provides better single-core performance and nearly matches the multi-core performance of the optional M4 Pro in the previous-generation Mac mini. Compared ot the standard M4 Mac mini, the new M6 version blows it away in CPU and SSD performance.
These are the kinds of generational improvements we’ve come to expect with Apple Silicon, which seems to be firing on all cylinders these days. The new Mac mini also gets other, less-highlighted improvements, like faster standard wired networking (2.5 GbE versus 1 GbE) and Wi-Fi 7/Bluetooth 6.0 instead of Wi-Fi 6E/Bluetooth 5.4.
However, the elephant in the room is pricing for the Mac mini. Earlier this year, you could grab a base Mac mini for $599 – although availability was spotty after Q1, thanks to OpenClaw and anticipated price hikes. More importantly, over the years, going from one Mac mini generation to the next typically yielded performance benefits with no (or minimal) price increase. The AI revolution has rewritten the hardware rulebook, so we’re now faced with a new generation that is $300 more expensive than the previous model ($200 June price increase + another $100 increase for this new generation).
So in a matter of months, what was for years a screaming bargain for anyone looking for a cheap entry point into the Mac desktop ecosystem has gotten a lot more expensive. 16GB of memory and a 256GB hard drive are easier to justify at $599, but it’s a tougher pill to swallow at $899, and especially so with our review unit’s as-tested price of $1,399.
Brandon Hill is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware. He has written about PC and Mac tech since the late 1990s with bylines at AnandTech, DailyTech, and Hot Hardware. When he is not consuming copious amounts of tech news, he can be found enjoying the NC mountains or the beach with his wife and two sons.
- 
VizzieTheViz A shame that the price has gone up so much, but that unfortunately is the case for competing small systems too (and larger systems and every other thing it seems).Reply
 
 Still if you need a small system and you can’t travel time to buy the $599 version you could do far worse.
 
The only alternatives I see are not buying a PC at all or paying a similar markup for a system from another brand.

articles.title: Von Bitcoin gelernt: EZB bringt Blockchain-Technologie in den regulären Wertpapierhandel
articles.text:
Von Bitcoin gelernt: EZB bringt Blockchain-Technologie in den regulären Wertpapierhandel
Die Europäische Zentralbank (EZB) und die nationalen Notenbanken des Euroraums wagen einen bedeutenden Schritt in die digitale Finanzzukunft. Mit dem Start der neuen Plattform namens Pontes ermöglicht das Eurosystem Finanzinstituten künftig, digitale Wertpapiere direkt mit sicherem Zentralbankgeld zu verrechnen. Gleichzeitig kündigte die EZB an, künftig selbst einen Teil ihrer eigenen Finanzmittel in solche neuartigen Papiere anzulegen, um die Technologie in der Praxis zu erproben.
Schnellere Geschäfte durch Tokenisierung
Bislang beruht der traditionelle Wertpapierhandel auf einer Kette von Zwischenstationen: Wer Anleihen oder Aktien kauft, durchläuft getrennte Prozesse von der Börse über Clearingstellen bis hin zur Verwahrung bei Spezialbanken. Durch die sogenannte Tokenisierung – bei der Vermögenswerte in Form digitaler Token auf Basis moderner Blockchain-Technologie (Distributed Ledger Technology, DLT) erfasst werden – lassen sich diese Schritte in einem einzigen, automatisierten Vorgang bündeln.
Diese dezentrale Datenbank-Technologie ist der breiten Öffentlichkeit bislang vor allem als technisches Fundament von Kryptowährungen wie Bitcoin bekannt. Sie findet nun aber zunehmend Einzug in die regulierte Finanzwelt. Das spart Zeit, verringert Kosten und senkt Risiken im Großkundengeschäft.
Zentralbankgeld als risikofreies Fundament
Allerdings fehlte auf diesen modernen Plattformen bislang ein zentraler Baustein: ein vollkommen sicheres und stabiles Zahlungsmittel. Genau hier setzt Pontes an, dessen Name sich vom lateinischen Wort für «Brücken» ableitet. Die Plattform fungiert als Verbindung zwischen der Welt der Blockchain-Netzwerke und dem klassischen Zentralbankgeld, das als risikofrei gilt. EZB-Präsidentin Christine Lagarde betonte, das Eurosystem arbeite daran, den europäischen Finanzmarkt im digitalen Zeitalter integrierter, innovativer und krisenfester aufzustellen. Nach Angaben von EZB-Direktoriumsmitglied Piero Cipollone bringt Pontes die notwendige Stabilität und das Vertrauen in die tokenisierte Finanzwelt, um dieser zum Durchbruch zu verhelfen.
Großbanken von Beginn an mit an Bord
Zum Start steht Pontes zunächst mit grundlegenden Funktionen bereit; bis 2028 soll das System schrittweise ausgebaut werden. Das Interesse aus der Finanzbranche ist bereits groß: Eine erste Gruppe führender Banken – darunter Institute wie die Deutsche Bank, die BayernLB, die DZ Bank sowie Förderbanken wie die KfW und die Europäische Investitionsbank – sowie Betreiber von DLT-Netzwerken haben sich der Plattform schon angeschlossen oder Vorbereitungen dafür abgeschlossen.
Notenbank investiert eigenes Geld
Um die Praxistauglichkeit nicht nur von außen zu begleiten, will die EZB zudem selbst als Anlegerin aktiv werden. Die Notenbank bereitet vor, einen kleinen Teil ihres sogenannten Eigenmittelportfolios – aus dem unter anderem laufende Betriebsausgaben bestritten werden – in tokenisierte Wertpapiere zu investieren. Die Notenbank will damit aus erster Hand Erfahrungen über den gesamten Lebenszyklus digitaler Wertpapiere sammeln und ein deutliches Signal für den Finanzstandort Europa setzen.

articles.title: Telus texting Pixel 10 Pro deal with $60/100GB plan to some Koodo customers
articles.text:
Telus is messaging some Koodo customers, offering a special deal if they switch to Telus.
Over the weekend, my wife received one such message from Telus, offering a Pixel 10 Pro for $5/mo financing along with a $60/100GB plan.
The financing portion of the deal is not much different from what Telus offers on its website right now. First, it uses Telus’ Bring-it-Back program, which means Telus discounts the monthly financing cost if customers agree to return the device after 24 months. Customers can also pay the difference at the end of their contract to keep the phone.
In the case of the Pixel 10 Pro, it breaks down like this. Telus charges $1,580 for the device, but takes away $1,460 of the cost, leaving customers with $120 in financing charges, or $5/mo for 24 months. The $1,460 is split into a $1,170 smartphone discount, an $80 Bring-it-Back bonus discount, and a $210 Bring-it-Back amount. That last part is what you’d pay at the end of your term to keep the device, for a total cost of $330 for the device. Compare that to the regular Pixel 10 Pro financing, which costs $17.08/mo (or $409.92 total over 24 months), and you’re actually saving a little over $100. Not bad!
But while the financing might not be different from the options on Telus website, the plan certainly is. The Telus offer includes a $60/100GB 5G+ Complete plan. However, looking at the options on Telus’ website right now, the 100GB 5G+ Complete plan costs $95/mo when paired with the Pixel 10 Pro.
So, that’s a savings of $35/mo for the plan alone, which is honestly very solid. I do think $60/100GB is a bit on the high side still, especially when you can get options like $45/125GB from carriers like Freedom Mobile, but it’s a good price for Telus.
Telus’ 5G+ Complete plan includes 100GB of shareable data with speeds of up to 2Gbps (and unlimited usage at throttled speeds of up to 512Kbps), unlimited talk and text in the U.S., unlimited long distance to 27 destinations, and more. The plan includes unlimited data roaming in the U.S., but with a limit of 5GB/day at full speed followed by unlimited use at up to 512Kbps.
The text offer also touts some other Telus benefits, like a five-year price lock, a free year of Skip+, and other exclusive benefits through Telus Rewards.
So, keep an eye on your text messages if you’re with Koodo, because Telus might soon offer you a half-decent upgrade option.

articles.title: X will now tell users when governments have forced it to limit their posts | TechCrunch
articles.text:
X on Monday announced it will now tell users when their posts have been “shadowbanned,” meaning shown to fewer people, due to the company’s compliance with local laws. The feature is an expansion of the social network’s earlier transparency tool called “Under the Hood,” which allows users to see if any labels have been applied to their account or their posts that could have affected their visibility on the platform.
It will also highlight any downranking of users’ posts due to government-required content filtering.
Previously, information about how an X user’s account or posts were being labeled and downranked was not available to end users. As a result, many often accused the company, formerly known as Twitter, of having shadowbanned them.
In addition, most companies that share data about government requests do so on an aggregate basis through “transparency reports,” not at the account or post level.
That began to change when, in August, X rolled out its transparency tool to offer more visibility into its moderation decisions. The “Under the Hood” option in the X app settings allows anyone who has posted at least 10 times during the month to download their aggregate stats as a JSON file, a standard data format. (Non-technical users can drop the file into any AI chatbot to have it explained.)
This same process will now show if an account or posts have had their visibility limited because X is complying with local laws. The file will also include which posts were withheld in a country following a legal demand, and which country made the request.
Governments cite a range of reasons for such demands, from laws against hate speech to terrorism-related content to election rules. Of course, critics, including free-expression groups, say some countries also use these laws to squash political dissent.
The update follows a number of other transparency-related efforts at X, including the open-sourcing of its “For You” algorithm, which selects the posts in users’ main feed, and an expansion of its efforts to open source parts of its codebase. The latter involved adding more detail, including on the model configuration, filtering, and core ranking system details. That means the code now includes the parameters used to weight different signals — information that is key to understanding which posts are actually displayed.
At the time of that open-sourcing effort, X’s vice president of product, Keith Coleman, said it was “the kind of thing that I think people will be fairly shocked that we are releasing.”

articles.title: 9 Must-read lessons about friendship from classic books
articles.text:
9 Must-read lessons about friendship from classic books
Discover 9 powerful friendship lessons from classic books that teach loyalty, trust, forgiveness, courage, and the value of true companionship.
Friendship is one of literature's most enduring themes. Long before social media and instant messaging connected people across the globe, authors were writing about companionship, loyalty, trust, and the challenges that come with maintaining meaningful relationships.
Classic books continue to resonate because the lessons they offer about friendship remain relevant regardless of age or era.
Whether it's standing by someone during difficult times, learning to forgive mistakes, or finding strength in a loyal companion, these stories remind us what true friendship looks like.
9 Timeless lessons about friendship from classic books
1. True friends stand by you in difficult times: Charlotte's Web by E.B. White
The friendship between Wilbur the pig and Charlotte the spider is one of the most touching relationships in children's literature. When Wilbur learns that his life is in danger, Charlotte does everything she can to save him.
Their bond teaches an important lesson: real friendship isn't measured by convenience. True friends support one another when challenges arise, even when helping requires sacrifice. Charlotte's loyalty shows that friendship is often revealed through actions rather than words.
2. Differences can strengthen a friendship: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes by Arthur Conan Doyle
Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson could hardly be more different. Holmes relies on logic and observation, while Watson brings empathy, practicality, and emotional intelligence.
Yet these differences are exactly what make their friendship work. Together, they balance each other's strengths and weaknesses. Their relationship reminds us that meaningful friendships don't require identical personalities; sometimes contrasting qualities create the strongest partnerships.
3. Friendship requires loyalty: The Lord of the Rings by J.R.R. Tolkien
Few friendships in literature are as inspiring as the bond between Frodo Baggins and Samwise Gamgee. Throughout their dangerous journey, Sam remains loyal despite exhaustion, fear, and uncertainty.
Their story demonstrates that loyalty is one of the foundations of lasting friendship. Being a good friend means showing up consistently, especially when circumstances become difficult. Friendship grows stronger when people remain dependable through adversity.
4. Friends help us become better people: Anne of Green Gables by L.M. Montgomery
Anne Shirley's friendship with Diana Barry becomes one of the most cherished relationships in classic literature. Together, they share adventures, dreams, mistakes, and personal growth.
Their friendship highlights how friends can encourage us to be more confident and courageous. Supportive relationships often help people discover talents and strengths they might never have recognised on their own.
5. Forgiveness is essential for lasting friendships: Little Women by Louisa May Alcott
The March sisters experience disagreements, jealousy, misunderstandings, and hurt feelings throughout the novel. Yet despite their conflicts, they repeatedly choose forgiveness and understanding.
No friendship is perfect. People make mistakes and occasionally disappoint one another. Little Women reminds readers that strong friendships survive because people learn to move beyond conflicts rather than allowing them to destroy the relationship.
6. Friendship can be a source of healing: The Secret Garden by Frances Hodgson Burnett
At the beginning of the novel, Mary Lennox is lonely, unhappy, and emotionally withdrawn. Through her growing friendships with Dickon and Colin, she gradually transforms into a happier and more compassionate person.
The story illustrates how genuine friendship can have a healing effect. Sometimes the support, encouragement, and companionship of others can help people overcome isolation and emotional struggles.
7. Friendship means accepting imperfections: Winnie-the-Pooh by A.A. Milne
Pooh and his friends have very different personalities. Eeyore is pessimistic, Tigger is energetic, Rabbit is organised, and Piglet is often anxious. Despite their differences, they continue to care for one another.
This classic story teaches that friendship isn't about finding perfect people. It's about accepting others for who they are, including their flaws, quirks, and unique characteristics.
8. Trust is earned through actions: The Wind in the Willows by Kenneth Grahame
Mole, Rat, Badger, and Toad share a friendship built on trust and mutual support. Even when Toad's reckless behaviour creates problems, his friends continue guiding him toward better choices.
Their relationship demonstrates that trust develops gradually through consistent actions. Friends earn confidence by being reliable, honest, and willing to help when needed.
9. Friendship is one of life's greatest treasures: The Great Gatsby by F. Scott Fitzgerald
Although The Great Gatsby is often remembered for its themes of ambition and the American Dream, the relationship between Gatsby and Nick Carraway offers another important lesson. Nick remains one of the few people willing to see Gatsby's humanity beneath the glamour and mystery.
The novel suggests that genuine friendship is rare and valuable. In a world often focused on status, success, and appearances, authentic human connections remain among life's greatest gifts.
Final thoughts
The best friendships aren't built overnight. They are strengthened through loyalty, understanding, patience, and shared experiences. Classic books remind us that friendship is not simply about having someone to spend time with; it's about finding people who support us, challenge us, and help us grow.
Whether it's Charlotte's sacrifice for Wilbur, Sam's loyalty to Frodo, or Anne's bond with Diana, these stories continue to offer lessons that remain just as meaningful today as when they were first written.

articles.title: Hausse du carburant : 3 applications gratuites indispensables pour trouver les stations les moins chères
articles.text:
Hausse du carburant : 3 applications gratuites indispensables pour trouver les stations les moins chères
Avec les prix du carburant qui repartent à la hausse, voici les meilleures applications mobiles gratuites pour trouver la station essence la moins onéreuse autour de soi.
Bienvenue à vous, cher automobiliste en véhicule thermique. Vous êtes au bon endroit, quelle que soit la situation présente. En effet, contexte exceptionnel ou non (au hasard : la situation géopolitique début 2026 et le prix du baril de pétrole en hausse à cause de la guerre en Iran), l'essence est toujours un bien onéreux sur lequel il n'est jamais perdu de tenter de faire quelques économies.
Pour économiser quelques euros à la pompe au quotidien ou durant un voyage, il y a assurément plus efficace que de rouler au hasard pour trouver une station un peu moins chère que les autres. En attendant qu'il bloque éventuellement les prix, le gouvernement propose le site prix-carburants. S'y trouve une carte interactive avec des filtres (type de carburant, lieu...).
Si cette solution est plutôt commode à utiliser en anticipation et depuis le confort d'un ordinateur ou le grand écran d'une tablette depuis chez soi, difficile d'en dire autant depuis son smartphone dans sa voiture qui crie soif. C'est là qu'interviennent différentes applications mobiles gratuites, qui en profitent pour ajouter quelques fonctionnalités souvent bien pratiques. Si elles ne font pas de miracles, puisqu'elles n'ont aucune influence sur les prix pratiqués à la pompe, ces apps peuvent cependant un peu compenser la hausse des prix tout en évitant une recherche fastidieuse.
Notez que nous avons retenu trois solutions complètes et populaires, fonctionnelles sur iOS et Android, mais que bien d'autres solutions alternatives existent. Toutes se ressemblent beaucoup, mais chacune avec ses petites spécificités a peut-être LA fonctionnalité qu'il vous faut. Relevons notamment : Fuel Flash, Fuelio, Gaspal et SLMC. Et si le carburant vous coûte toujours trop cher, adopter une conduite plus souple peu légèrement réduire la consommation, tandis que passer à un véhicule hybride ou électrique est peut être le moment.
Essence&Co
Capable d'afficher les stations les moins chères autour de soi via une carte ou la géolocalisation, Essence&Co est l'une des applications du genre les plus utilisées. Il faut dire qu'au-delà de son interface claire et de sa recherche par critères complète, l'application se repose sur sa communauté pour tenir à jour les prix affichés.
Conçue en France, l'application propose de nombreuses informations pour faire le meilleur choix, y compris les types de carburant et de services de chaque station. Une fois une station choisie via une carte ou une liste, il est également possible de mettre en place un itinéraire avec votre application GPS préférée.
Essence/Gasoil Now
Si la précédente proposition ne vous convient pas, direction Essence/Gasoil Now. Cette application propose peu ou prou la même chose, mais dans une interface un peu plus minimaliste et qui va davantage à l'essentiel (le carburant). Il n'est aussi plus question de la mise à jour des prix par la communauté, mais cette dernière peut indiquer quand une station est épuisée.
Si les utilisateurs semblent satisfaits de la solution, les derniers commentaires critiquent en revanche la multiplication de publicités pénibles au sein de l'application. À vous de voir si la pénibilité en vaut le plein.
Roole Map
Alors que le logiciel GPS très populaire Waze permet d'afficher le prix des carburants, profitons de cette sélection pour enfin évoquer Roole Map. Française, cette application se rêve comme une alternative à Waze et à Google Maps. Ainsi, en plus d'afficher les stations les plus proches ou les moins chères autour de soi (cela reste tout de même l'objectif premier de cet article), l'application propose bien d'autres choses.
Itinéraire, indications d'événements (radars, accidents, traffic...), compatibilité Android Auto, suivi des bornes de recharge ou encore affichage des aires d'autoroute et des parkings, Roole Map se veut très complète et, évidemment, gratuite. Peut-être que dans votre quête du carburant le moins cher vous venez également de trouver une alternative aux solutions GPS de Google.
Roole Map
Application tout-en-un pour votre véhicule thermique, hybride ou électrique.
- Systèmes d'exploitation : macOS, Android
- Catégories : Information, Voyage

articles.title: Acheter un PC maintenant ou attendre 2027 ? La réponse du patron d'Acer
articles.text:
La flambée de la mémoire vive dicte depuis des mois le prix de tout ce qui embarque une puce, du smartphone à la console en passant par les ordinateurs. Dans un entretien accordé le 19 septembre, Jason Chen, président et directeur général d’Acer, s’est risqué à un exercice que ses homologues évitent soigneusement : donner des dates. Son calendrier a le mérite d’être précis, et le défaut de contredire une partie de ce que l’industrie répète depuis des mois.
Une dernière marche avant le sommet
Le quatrième trimestre 2026 commencera par une hausse, que Chen évalue entre 5 et 20 % selon les configurations. Les machines gavées de mémoire et de stockage SSD trinqueront le plus, ce qui tombe mal pour quiconque lorgnait un PC bien équipé sous le sapin. Les fêtes se feront donc au tarif fort, sans que cela marque la fin de l’ascension : le dirigeant situe le pic des prix de vente moyens vers la mi-2027, avant une possible décrue au second semestre.
Ce décalage tient à la mécanique du secteur. Entre le moment où un composant baisse chez le fournisseur et celui où l’étiquette bouge en rayon, plusieurs mois s’écoulent, le temps d’assembler, d’expédier et d’écouler les stocks achetés au prix fort. Un prix de PC, ça freine comme un paquebot. Chen compte sur les capacités de production de mémoire supplémentaires attendues l’an prochain pour amorcer la manœuvre dès le début de 2027.
Le patron d’Acer s’offre au passage un contre-pied assumé : « il est impossible que la pénurie se prolonge jusqu’en 2030 », balaie-t-il, alors que ce scénario catastrophe circulait encore cet été dans l’industrie. Il assure même que les fournisseurs de composants frappent désormais à sa porte pour vendre, signe que l’offre repasse doucement devant la demande. Le rapport de force a basculé.
La mémoire ne manque plus, vraiment ?
Voilà l’affirmation la plus audacieuse de l’entretien : d’après Chen, la DDR4 et la DDR5 ne manquent plus vraiment, et les processeurs redeviennent disponibles, entrée de gamme mise à part. Les analystes du secteur décrivent pourtant un tout autre paysage. TrendForce estimait fin juillet que l’offre mondiale de DRAM resterait inférieure à la demande jusqu’en 2027 inclus, les nouvelles usines ne produisant en volume qu’à partir de 2028. Le même cabinet anticipe encore 13 à 18 % de hausse sur la mémoire pour serveurs entre le deuxième et le troisième trimestre 2026.
Les deux discours se réconcilient à condition de regarder où la pénurie s’est installée : dans les baies de serveurs, où l’IA et la mémoire HBM engloutissent les capacités des usines, pendant que la demande grand public s’essouffle. Les fabricants de PC récupèrent les miettes du festin, des miettes disponibles, certes, mais facturées au prix fort. Chen décrit donc fidèlement son propre canal d’approvisionnement (et un peu moins la santé globale du marché).
Rappelons aussi que le dirigeant est tout sauf un observateur neutre. Acer négocie ses achats de composants en ce moment même, et déclarer publiquement que rien ne manque reste une façon élégante de peser sur les tarifs de ses fournisseurs.
