articles.title: Verschwindet für lange Zeit: Diesen Planeten können Astronomen nur noch sieben Jahre beobachten
articles.text:
Verschwindet für lange Zeit: Diesen Planeten können Astronomen nur noch sieben Jahre beobachten
Auf der Suche nach außergewöhnlichen Exoplaneten sind Forscher:innen der Uni Tokio auf einen seltsamen Riesenplaneten gestoßen. Bei TOI-1355 b handelt es sich um einen sogenannten heißen Super-Jupiter. Der Planet verfügt über knapp die sechsfache Masse des Jupiter und ist 1,4-mal so groß.
Heißer Super-Jupiter mit seltsamem Orbit
Wie das Forschungsteam um Noriharu Watanabe und Norio Narita anhand der Analyse von Daten des Tess-Weltraumteleskops herausgefunden hat, kreist der Exoplanet innerhalb von nur gut zwei Tagen um seinen Stern. Dieser ist mit 8.400 Grad Celsius fast 3.000 Grad heißer als unsere Sonne.
Eigentlich, so die Astronom:innen, müsste TOI-1355 b eine kreisförmige Umlaufbahn um seinen Stern haben. Aber anders als bei heißen Jupitern, die um heiße Sterne kreisen, ist der Orbit elliptisch. Für Watanabe und Narita ein Grund, den Planeten im Detail zu erforschen, wie es in einer Mitteilung der Uni Tokio heißt.
Interaktion mit anderen Riesenplaneten
Schließlich könnte die Entdeckung eines heißen Jupiters mit sehr exzentrischer Umlaufbahn die Theorie stützen, dass solche Planeten, die um heiße Sterne kreisen, mit anderen Planeten interagieren. Die durch weitere Riesenplaneten möglicherweise erzeugte stark elliptische Bahn könnte durch Gezeiten später nach und nach weiter verkleinert werden und sich abrunden.
Im Rahmen der Untersuchungen stellten die Forscher:innen aber fest, dass TOI-1355 b sich nur noch rund sieben Jahre lang von der Erde aus beobachten lässt. Mitte 2033 könnte er aus der Sichtlinie verschwinden, in der er aus unserer Perspektive heraus vor seinem Stern vorbeizieht, wie es bei scinexx.de heißt. Über die sogenannte Transitmethode könnte er dann für mehrere Jahrhunderte für Astronom:innen nicht mehr sichtbar sein.
Astronomen wollen Webb-Weltraumteleskop nutzen
Innerhalb der kommenden sieben Jahre bieten sich derweil über 1.000 Transfers für weitere Beobachtungen an, wenn die entsprechenden Bedingungen wie Wetter und Licht stimmen und Teleskope verfügbar sind. Die Astronom:innen der Uni Tokio wollen eigenen Angaben nach etwa beim James-Webb-Weltraumteleskop der Nasa anfragen.

articles.title: A cut cable disrupted hundreds of flights across the US
articles.text:
Hundreds of flights were cancelled or delayed on Monday after construction crews in New Jersey accidentally cut a Verizon fiber cable used for air traffic control.
A cut cable disrupted hundreds of flights across the US
The line has been repaired, but delays are ongoing.
FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said that a circuit failure led to the discovery of the severed fiber cable, ABC News reports. The outage hammered airports across the Northeast, causing ground stops at all three major New York City airports.
In a statement to CNBC, Verizon said that it bore “no responsibility for this incident,” putting the blame on “construction contractors working in the area” that “dug up and cut our cable.”
Ironically, it looks like trains make have taken out the planes, but fingers are still being pointed. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said an Amtrak crew accidentally cut the line, but AP reports that Amtrak blames a New Jersey Transit crew for the disruption. “This incident occurred on New Jersey Transit property and involved a New Jersey Transit contractor,” an Amtrak spokesperson told NBC4.
As of Monday evening, Duffy said that “the telecom lines have been repaired, and all airport operations in the Northeast are resuming,” but cautioned that it will take “some time to clear all existing delays.” According to FlightAware, there were over 1,000 canceled flights today in the US

articles.title: Marvel cancela 'Daredevil Born Again': la serie no volverá después de su tercera temporada
articles.text:
Disney ha puesto el último clavo en el ataúd de Daredevil: Born Again. La tercera temporada será la última de la serie, luego de que su showrunner, Dario Scardapane, dejara el proyecto en plena posproducción. La decisión forma parte de una reestructuración de Marvel Studios, en donde dejarán de invertir en series de televisión para enfocarse de nuevo en la pantalla grande.
De acuerdo con The Hollywood Reporter, Daredevil: Born Again llegará a su fin con la tercera temporada. A dos meses de que concluyera su rodaje, la serie basada en el popular superhéroe ya no continuará. Disney decidió no renovar el contrato de Scarpadane, quien tomó las riendas del proyecto luego de trabajar en The Punisher para Netflix.
Aunque Marvel Studios intentó enderezar el barco, la realidad es que la serie de Daredevil nunca consiguió repetir el éxito que obtuvo en Netflix. El proyecto tuvo un recorrido bastante accidentado desde su llegada a Disney+, comenzando con el plan inicial que se alejaba de la temática oscura y temas más maduros que hicieron famosa a la versión original. Las huelgas de 2023 fueron clave para que el estudio reiniciara el proyecto y se deshiciera de los guionistas originales, Matt Corman y Chris Ord, quienes apostaban por una serie más "light".
El cambio de rumbo también afectó al formato de la serie. Originalmente, la primera temporada tendría 18 episodios, pero tras el reinicio Marvel Studios redujo la cuota a 17 y los dividió en dos temporadas. La historia continuaría años después de los sucesos ocurridos en la serie de Netflix, con un Wilson Fisk tomando las riendas como alcalde de Nueva York y listo para vengarse de Matt Murdock y compañía.
La tercera temporada de Daredevil: Born Again será la última
La trama de la tercera temporada continúa con Fisk cargando contra todos los superhéroes que se cruzan en su camino. Si hacemos memoria, la segunda temporada cerró con el encarcelamiento de Daredevil, quien expuso su identidad secreta y ahora tendrá que lidiar con ello tras las rejas.
Aunque la próxima temporada será la última, el reparto promete un cierre por todo lo alto. Ya en los últimos capítulos habíamos visto al elenco de The Defenders con Krysten Ritter recuperando el papel de Jessica Jones y un cameo de Mike Colter como Luke Cage. Unas fotografías filtradas durante el rodaje de la tercera temporada mostraron a Finn Jones, quien regresa en su papel de Iron Fist para completar el grupo de superhéroes y enfrentar a un Kingpin ya despojado de su cargo como alcalde.
Se espera que la temporada final de Daredevil: Born Again se estrene en Disney+ en 2027, cerrando así un capítulo que comenzó hace más de una década en Netflix y que ha sobrevivido a cancelaciones, reinicios y cambios de guionistas antes de despedirse definitivamente.
Con el fin de sus series de televisión, Marvel centrará sus esfuerzos en la pantalla grande. El primer bombazo llegará con Avengers: Doomsday en diciembre de 2026 y un año más tarde repetirá la dosis con Avengers: Secret Wars. Otros proyectos que se encuentran en la lista son la película de Ghost Rider con Ryan Gosling y el esperado reboot de los X-Men, así como Black Panther 3.

articles.title: Google's $899 Googlebook is a bet that you'll buy a new laptop for Gemini | TechCrunch
articles.text:
After first unveiling its new AI-powered laptop, dubbed Googlebook, in May, Google on Monday said the new device is now available for preorder for $899.
Meant to offer a step up from traditional Chromebooks, Googlebooks run on Android OS with a desktop version of the Chrome browser and other familiar ChromeOS elements. However, the real pull for the new devices is that they’ll prominently feature Gemini’s latest capabilities in a new format: the laptop.
Google is trying to offer a laptop with unique features like an AI-powered cursor, vibe-coded widgets, and support for AI-enhanced dictation. The latter is a feature called Rambler, which cleans up messy, rambling brain dumps into readable text.
The move is a bet that AI, specifically Google’s Gemini, could be enough of a draw to get people to buy a new laptop that bakes in AI instead of running them via desktop apps you install or access through the browser. In addition, the devices could eventually replace Chromebooks, bringing millions of former Chromebook customers to Gemini AI.
On the Googlebook, Google is trying to reinvent the “point-and-click” experience of desktop computing to now include an AI element: The cursor serves as a conduit to Gemini. The company suggests various ways this could be used, like highlighting content on a web page for Gemini to work with, asking Gemini to see if an email you’ve hovered your cursor over is suspicious, or selecting images and then asking Gemini to visualize them together.
In practice, this feature isn’t very different from Android’s “Circle to Search,” which allows smartphone owners to use gestures like circling, highlighting, or tapping to connect with Google Search, which of course, also includes AI. While it’s a clever way to take advantage of the ways people use their phones, Circle to Search on its own didn’t inspire a mass exodus to Android.
Similarly, Magic Cursor, as the AI pointer is called, won’t likely be a main selling point for the Googlebook, especially now that we have AI agents that can take over your computer and browser to do tasks for you.
Google’s Rambler, however, may be one of the best of the AI features in this upgrade, as it meets a surprisingly useful need. However, this, too, isn’t enough reason to buy a new device, as it feels more like a feature that’s nice to have than a necessity.
Vibe-coding widgets are a minor addition, as well. Other Googlebook features, like Gemini Spark and Gemini Live, also don’t require special, new hardware.
What’s more interesting about the Googlebook is how it’s seemingly part of Google’s longer-term plan to capture a large part of the K-12 market that currently relies on Chromebooks and push them toward the company’s Gemini AI. There are somewhere around 50 million Chromebooks in schools, used by students and educators, Google has said.
In May, the company told TechCrunch that its current Chromebooks would continue to be supported, though many would become eligible to transition to the new Googlebook experience in the future.
The $899 device will include 12 months of Google AI Pro, which gives you 5TB of cloud storage, Gemini Advanced tools, and 3 months of YouTube Premium, Adobe Photoshop, and more. The devices will receive regular updates for up to 10 years, Google said.
Googlebook preorders are open now on the Google Store and at Best Buy and other retailers. Devices will hit shelves on October 4 in the U.S. and on October 5 in Canada, the U.K., Ireland, France, Germany, and Australia.
Flagship devices in the new range are being built by Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, and Lenovo, with materials like aluminum, magnesium alloy, and carbon fiber. They feature up to 2.8K OLED displays, haptic glass trackpads, and backlit keyboards. Under the hood, they’ll run on processors from Intel and Qualcomm paired with dedicated NPUs. Google says the device will offer up to 14 hours of battery life.

articles.title: Cloudflare saves 100 TB of RAM again, this time by slashing server hashes by 90% — cutting 100,000 entries down to 10,000 eliminates massive cache bloat
articles.text:
Cloudflare saves 100 TB of RAM again, this time by slashing server hashes by 90% — cutting 100,000 entries down to 10,000 eliminates massive cache bloat
A perfect illustration of an optimization for memory, after an optimization for speed
Cloudflare has saved 100 TB of RAM again, but this time by tuning its hash-mapping algorithm. One of Cloudflare's largest business use cases is data caching, more specifically serving a URL directly from memory or disk instead of fetching it from the live site, which may take a significant amount of time. The company uses its own open-source Pingora framework for the task of mapping an arbitrary URL to one of its cadre of cache servers, using the Ketama algorithm. This task is simple in concept, but can get quite tricky in an environment where it's expected that backend servers appear and disappear — and harder still when done at Cloudflare's scale.
"Backend routing," or the mapping of a URL to one of many cached servers, requires a lot of tables held in memory. An incoming URL is hashed (like you do with files with CRC-32), and that resulting number is taken and sent out to a server. The first instinct is to do this sequentially, one URL per server, but you hit the first problem: the same URLs aren't going to the same servers. So what you do is you make a hash corresponding to the server, say with its IP address and name, and match both hashes together by numerical proximity.
That sounds simple, and it works fine, as the URL hashes' distribution is going to be effectively random, and the requests will be redirected to the same server in an egalitarian way. But then you run face-first against the second problem: say you have four servers serving 25% of requests each, and #2 disappears because someone tripped on the power cable. You'll be forced to redirect the requests it handled onto whichever are closest in the hash map, and end up overloading server #3, the next one over, while #1 and #4 remain under little load.
The solution to that is to add more hashes per server and mix them up randomly. Now your four servers' many hashes have a random distribution, and if one dies, incoming requests should be equally distributed among the remaining ones. This takes a lot of memory, and it takes far more once you set up layers with weight rules (so that bigger servers handle more requests), and the fact that, due to content restrictions and architectural regions, not all servers can serve all requests. All told, Cloudflare was running with as many as 100,000 server hashes per machine, ballooning RAM requirements.
After judicious application of some algebra and basic statistics, Cloudflare engineers concluded that using those 100,000 hashes was far and away beyond the point of diminishing returns. The team calculated that a mere 10% of that amount was good enough for nearly the same results, as the error rate barely drops for each order of magnitude beyond 10,000. After some judicious wrangling of Rust's data structures to save 2 bytes per entry in the hash-server map. That sounds like nothing, but it quickly adds up with billions of records.
All things considered, the Cloudflare team saved around 100 TB of RAM total with this optimization. To play it safe, the team added this "v2" algorithm as a separate code path rather than replacing the code altogether — allowing them to simply swap back to the original one if something broke. Now if only all modern software were this judicious about resource usage.

Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: Egypt’s Bekia raises $765k to scale recycling economy tech - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Egyptian startup Bekia, which is digitising waste collection, has raised a US$765,000 seed round to deepen its consumer app and launch its first B2B software product.
Founded in 2019, Bekia is a digital platform building the collection layer for Egypt’s recycling economy. The platform began with a consumer app – a household books a pickup, a collector arrives at a scheduled time, material is weighed on the spot at a published rate, and payment goes to a bank account or digital wallet.
At the end of October, Bekia will launch Bekia Next, which turns that data into verified CO₂-avoidance certificates for corporate clients using established international carbon accounting methodology. It is the first thing Bekia sells as a subscription rather than a service.
The startup’s US$765,000 funding round is led by Madica, the Africa-focused investment programme affiliated with Flourish Ventures, and also features Catalyst Fund and Dakar-based Jambaar Capital. Bekia will use the funding to grow its engineering team, take Bekia Next to market, and begin testing the model in a second African market.
“Egypt’s recycling sector has always worked — it just worked invisibly, on cash and trust, with no record of any of it,” said Alaa Afifi, founder and CEO of Bekia. “We built the software layer that changes that: a collector gets a transaction history, a factory gets traceable supply, a household learns what its waste is actually worth. The material itself is a commodity, but the record of it isn’t, and nobody in our market owns that record yet.”
“What excites us about Bekia is how the team is drawing on its firsthand understanding of waste collection in Egypt to build a more interconnected, tech-driven ecosystem serving households, small businesses and large industrial waste producers,” said Emmanuel Adegboye, head of Madica. “We’re proud to welcome them to the Madica programme and support that ambition with long-term capital, company-building expertise and networks.”

articles.title: Govt asks Microsoft to set up data centres closer to power generation sites
articles.text:
Govt asks Microsoft to set up data centres closer to power generation sites
Microsoft on Monday formally launched its fourth India cloud region, in Hyderabad, as part of its $20.5 billion investment commitment to the country's digital and AI infrastructure.
The government on Monday asked Microsoft to locate future data centres closer to power generation sources rather than near cable landing stations, with Electronics and IT Secretary S Krishnan saying this would cut costs for both the company and the country.
Speaking at the launch of Microsoft's fourth India cloud region in Hyderabad, Krishnan said it was easier and more economical to build data centres near power sources than near coastal cable landing hubs such as Chennai.
"It will be much more economical if you go closer to where the power itself is generating," he said, adding that the government would continue to facilitate faster approvals to meet the requirements of both the country and the world.
Microsoft on Monday formally launched its fourth India cloud region, in Hyderabad, as part of its $20.5 billion investment commitment to the country's digital and AI infrastructure.
The India South Central region, which became generally available on August 6, joins the company's existing regions in Pune, Chennai and Mumbai.
Krishnan called the launch significant for strengthening India's data centre and AI infrastructure, and said the country needs to simultaneously access the best global technology and build domestic, sovereign computing capacity.
He said India's scale of 1.4 billion people, along with its growing digital public infrastructure, generates large volumes of data that form a "treasure house" for AI applications, giving the country the potential to become "the application powerhouse of the world".
Krishnan said India's tax policies, ease of doing business, and the new telecom law permitting easier interconnection of facilities had made it simpler to build and connect a data centre to the grid in India than in many other countries.
The Hyderabad facility uses effectively zero water for cooling, relying on air-cooled chillers instead of traditional water-based systems, Microsoft India and South Asia President Puneet Chandok said.
He noted that the country has about 2 GW of data centre capacity, which is set to rise to 6-7 GW by 2035, with over $100 billion in investments already committed.
India would emerge as an AI infrastructure hub not just for itself but for Asia and the Global South, Chandok said.
In a video message, Microsoft Vice Chair and President Brad Smith said the new region would give organisations in India, and more broadly Asia, more capacity, greater resilience and more choice.
The expansion comes at a time of rapid digital growth in the country.
According to data from research firm IDC, India's public cloud services spending is forecast to reach $45.7 billion by 2030, growing at an annual rate of 22.2%, with AI spending expected to grow at double that pace.

articles.title: Lin Tsung-chi fundó una empresa de herrajes para muebles. Entonces llegó la IA y se convirtió en el hombre más rico de Taiwán
articles.text:
Cuando se habla del dinero que está generando la IA, habitualmente surgen los mismos nombres: Nvidia, OpenAI, Anthropic y sus nuevos fundadores milmillonarios. Sin embargo, al hablar de los enormes beneficios de la IA nadie piensa en un cajón de cocina. Ahí está la clave.
Kaohsiung es una ciudad portuaria del sur de Taiwán. Allí, se fundó una empresa que fabricaba tiradores para las puertas de los muebles. Para sorpresa de todos, su octogenario fundador, Lin Tsung-chi, se ha convertido en el hombre más rico de Taiwán y en uno de los más ricos del planeta.
De los cajones a los servidores. Lin Tsung-chi fundó King Slide en 1986 con el objetivo de fabricar herrajes para muebles aprovechando el gran boom de la construcción en China. En el año 2000, un cliente que sostenía el 40% de la facturación de King Slide exigió una rebaja del 30% en sus pedidos. Ante la negativa de Lin Tsung-chi de rebajar tanto sus precios, la compañía afrontó un serio revés en sus ingresos del año siguiente.
Según contaba Finance, esa crisis provocó que King Slide perdiera casi la mitad de su plantilla, poniendo en riesgo la viabilidad de la compañía. Esa necesidad hizo que Lin Tsung-chi buscara nuevos mercados para sus productos y encontró uno inesperado: las guías deslizantes para las bandejas en las que se montan los servidores en los armarios de los centros de datos.
Soporta todo el peso de la IA. King Slide no tardó en recibir importantes pedidos de Compaq e IBM. Hoy fabrica los raíles por los que se deslizan los millones invertidos en GPUs y memoria RAM de los grandes centros de datos de todo el mundo.
Por poner un ejemplo, sus guías deslizantes sustentan las bandejas del rack GB200 NVL72 de Nvidia que reúne 72 GPU, y nadie quiere verlo en el suelo. "Las GPU son demasiado caras para arriesgarse a que se caigan. Nuestros raíles garantizan que eso nunca ocurra", recogió la revista CommonWealth Magazine de boca de Jane Lin, hija del fundador y actual presidenta de la compañía. "Cuando llegó la ola de la IA, estábamos listos", aseguraba JC Wang, yerno del fundador. Se calcula que controla más del 70 % de los raíles de gama alta para servidores de IA.
Más margen que Nvidia o TSMC. Los datos financieros de King Slide son sorprendentes ya que el margen que dejan las guías de los servidores supera incluso a los que están teniendo las empresas que fabrican el hardware que sostiene. La cifra que lo disparó todo llegó el pasado agosto.
En el segundo trimestre, King Slide logró un margen bruto del 87,4%. Nvidia, con sus chips, se quedó en el 75%. Entre enero y julio, además, la firma facturó 22.690 millones de dólares taiwaneses (el equivalente a 622,80 millones de euros), lo que representa un 136,58% más que el ejercicio anterior. Su beneficio por acción de esos siete meses ya superaba al de todo 2025. En los últimos cuatro años, la empresa ha crecido un 3.279,6%, pasando de una valoración de 1.300 millones de dólares a 43.100 millones de dólares, según datos publicados por Bloomberg.
La bolsa haciendo su magia. Las acciones de King Slide se dispararon en agosto superando los 10.000 dólares taiwaneses, disparando a su vez la estimación de la fortuna de su fundador y principal accionista.
Según la lista en tiempo real de Forbes, Lin Tsung-chi sumó 1.800 millones de dólares en una sola jornada y su patrimonio llegó a 19.500 millones de dólares superando a Pierre Chen, fundador de Yageo (que precisamente fabrica componentes electrónicos para los centros de datos), y pasó a ser la persona más rica de Taiwán. En la actualidad, Lin Tsung-chi suma una fortuna estimada de 18.300 millones de dólares, manteniendo su liderazgo, aunque la cotización de las acciones de King Slide se haya moderado.
Llueve oro, pero muy rápido. "Es como si llovieran lingotes de oro del cielo", explicó Jane Lin a Bloomberg. El problema es que los lingotes caen a "una velocidad increíble. Si no eres lo bastante rápido, no podrás atraparlos", añadió. Además, nadie sabe cuánto durará la lluvia y llegará la época de sequía.
El debate sobre el ritmo de la IA ha desatado ventas en las acciones de las tecnológicas. Lin Tsung-chi admite que, como superviviente de aquella crisis del 2000, "todos los días estoy contento y preocupado a la vez. Mi mayor preocupación es que no podamos desarrollar a tiempo el producto de la próxima generación".
Los otros vendedores de palas. En la fiebre del oro de California de finales del siglo XIX, no solo se enriquecieron quienes encontraron un filón del dorado metal. Sobre todo, hicieron fortuna quienes como Levi Strauss o Samuel Brannan, vendían pantalones tejanos y palas a los buscadores. La historia de Lin Tsung-chi la fiebre de la IA tienen mucho en común con aquellos pioneros. Ahora las "palas" son raíles, brocas o memoria RAM.
En China, Guangdong Dtech fabrica microbrocas para agujerear las placas de los servidores. Es la mayor del mundo en su ramo por volumen de ventas, y su fundador, Wang Xin, tiene un patrimonio valorado en unos 11.600 millones de dólares. Bloomberg ha contabilizado al menos siete casos de "vendedores de palas" de la IA, con más de 62.000 millones de riqueza extra para sus accionistas. En Taiwán, las 50 mayores fortunas sumaron un récord de 308.000 millones.

articles.title: Google Hit With $463 Million Fine for EU Location Data Rule Breach
articles.text:
Google has been fined 403 million euros ($463 million) for breaching the European Union’s strict privacy rules because it mishandled users’ location data, the bloc’s data privacy watchdog said Monday.
Ireland’s Data Protection Commission said its investigation found Google did not lawfully or fairly process location data in users’ Web & App Activity, a Google setting that tracks browsing and search history, and in their Location History, a service that maps places they’ve been with their mobile phones.
Regulators also found the company failed to be lawful, fair and transparent when it processed personal data in its Location Accuracy feature in the Android mobile operating system.
Ireland is the lead regulator for Google in the 27-nation EU because the U.S. tech giant’s European headquarters is based in Dublin.
The investigation, which opened six years ago, examined how Google applied the EU privacy rule book, known as the General Data Protection Regulation, from the time it took effect in 2018 until February 2020.
“This case centers around historical policies that have since been updated,” Google said in a statement. “From 2019 onwards, we’ve significantly evolved our practices and launched robust tools that make managing location data simple.”
Regulators said that location data is a type of personal data that’s collected by Google and can be used to infer someone’s location.
“Location data can bring both benefits and harms to individuals,” Deputy Commissioner Graham Doyle said. “It can greatly enhance the utility of online services, but it can also reveal a significant amount of information about an individual, including information that is inherently private.”
It’s the fourth biggest EU privacy fine issued by the Irish watchdog, which has previously handed out bigger fines to TikTok and Meta, including a 1.2 billion euro fine for Meta.
The regulator said it still has three other ongoing privacy investigations involving Google.
Related: Dior, Louis Vuitton, Tiffany Fined $25 Million in South Korea After Data Breaches
Related: TikTok Reaches $400 Million Settlement With US Justice Department Over Children’s Privacy
Related: Uber Fined Nearly $1 Billion by Dutch Regulators Over Automated Suspensions of Driver Accounts

articles.title: The 20 European investors funding NATO’s defence and innovation | EU-Startups
articles.text:
NATO’s Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic (DIANA) has announced the first 24 investors who are joining the NATO DIANA Capital Network (NDCN), among which 20 are European-based – including Bpifrance, DTCP, and Project A.
The NDCN is a community of NATO-aligned investors whose aim will be to help scale innovative solutions critical to Allied security.
“The NATO DIANA Capital Network is a critical enabler of the Alliance’s technological and defensive edge,” says NATO DIANA Acting Managing Director Jyoti Hirani-Driver. “By connecting NATO-aligned capital and promising innovators, the network helps the best technologies move to real-world capabilities in a secure and values-based ecosystem. We are proud to welcome the network’s first 24 investors and look forward to growing this community across the Alliance.”
The launch of the NATO DIANA Capital Network comes amid substantial capital deployment into European defence and dual-use technology in 2026.
EU-Startups has seen approximately €1.73 billion across ten company financings this year, led by Munich-based Quantum Systems’ €1 billion Series D, ICEYE’s €450 million Series F in Finland and London-based Kraken Technology Group’s €152.9 million Series B.
Smaller rounds have also backed missile manufacturing, autonomous aerial intelligence, drone-defence lasers, unmanned-systems software and strategic advanced materials.
Several members of the new network are already active across these financings: DTCP led investments in Kraken and Norway’s Six Robotics, while the NATO Innovation Fund participated in rounds for Kraken, Greenjets and Uplift360 and led Kelluu’s €15 million Series A.
Kelluu is also a direct link to DIANA, having completed two phases of the NATO accelerator before its 2026 financing.
Alongside company-level investment, EU-Startups has covered dedicated 2026 defence and resilience vehicles including DTCP’s €500 million Project Liberty, the €500 million E2D fund and Lakestar’s €262.2 million Resilience I Fund, pointing to a broader build-out of specialised capital for European defence and dual-use technologies.
The NDCN was launched in April 2026 and is a curated, NATO-screened community of trusted investors committed to backing the dual-use and DeepTech companies emerging from the DIANA programme.
Members are sovereign and sovereign-backed funds, leading venture capital firms, family offices, and institutional investors drawn from across the 32 NATO Allied nations. The NDCN provides its members with structured access to DIANA’s screened company pipeline, direct connections to fellow Alliance investors, invitations to closed convenings with NATO leadership and end-users, and a zero-fee model from DIANA itself.
The NDCN forms part of the wider NATO DIANA network, which finds and accelerates cutting-edge technologies to deliver battle-winning defence and security solutions for the Alliance, while fostering DeepTech innovation.
DIANA will welcome more investors in the NDCN towards the end of the year.
NDCN members will have opportunities to engage with DIANA-validated innovators; companies whose technologies have already been tested and de‑risked against NATO and Allied capability needs.
Divided by European country of origin, the 24 inaugural investors are:

articles.title: The Download: investigating deaths at the US border’s “virtual wall”
articles.text:
The Download: investigating deaths at the US border’s “virtual wall”
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
The US spent billions on border surveillance. Why can’t it catch people before they die?
When José Morales Bernal crossed the border into the US in April 2024, the day before his 32nd birthday, he was within range of three surveillance towers equipped with cameras and AI to automatically detect and track people.
If the system worked as intended, Morales should have been apprehended. If he needed medical help, agents were trained to provide it. None of that happened.
Instead, Morales died just 360 feet from the closest tower. It was local landfill workers, rather than Border Patrol, who first spotted him. An autopsy concluded that he had died of “environmental exposure.”
A first-of-its-kind investigation by MIT Technology Review reveals that deaths like Morales’s are startlingly common. After mapping nearly 4,000 locations where human remains were found against information on nearly 600 surveillance towers, we discovered that a humanitarian crisis at the border has unfolded in view of the government’s own cameras.
Read our full investigation into the deadly failings of the virtual wall.
—James O'Donnell and Eileen Guo
Learn more:
- As part of our 15-month investigation, we created the first comprehensive map of deaths near US-Mexico border surveillance towers. Take a look at that map, and read about how we made it.
- The US government is about to spend another $1 billion to triple the virtual wall’s size, yet we found it has systemic flaws: broken towers, algorithms that failed to detect people and agents who simply did not respond to alerts. Here are four ideas for what Customs and Border Protection should do to rectify those failures.
- An analysis by the Times of San Diego found at least 138 cases since 2022 in which migrants’ remains were found within the nominal range of a nearby surveillance tower. A separate MIT Technology Review analysis estimated that more than half of those people were likely within a tower’s field of view. Gómez Hernández was one of them. Here’s her story, written by our partners at Times of San Diego.
All of these stories are part of Dying on Camera, our new series investigating the failures of border surveillance technology and their human cost.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 An AI hallucination nearly triggered a US military operation
A false report prompted plans to intercept a Chinese vessel. (CNN)
+ The incident comes as the Pentagon accelerates its use of AI. (Ars Technica)
+ “Humans in the loop” in AI war is an illusion. (MIT Technology Review)
2 Gemini has carried out Google’s first known autonomous AI hack
Google says the behavior wasn’t “misaligned” because its safety measures caught it. (WSJ $)
+ Here’s why AI agents cheat to reach their goals. (MIT Technology Review)
3 The US has proposed an AI safety alert system with China
It would flag AI incidents that pose national security risks. (AP)
+ Trump and Xi will consider the proposal at their summit this week. (NBC News)
+ Could AI really kill us all? (MIT Technology Review)
4 California’s governor has ordered work on an AI “kill switch”
It’s part of Gavin Newsom’s executive order on AI safety. (NBC News)
+ The order also calls for independent oversight of AI companies. (NYT $)
5 Data centers are turning to forever chemicals for cooling
PFAS cooling can reduce water use but raises pollution risks. (Fortune)
+ US regulators are fast-tracking PFAS for data center cooling. (The Hill)
6 Iran and China used AI agents to automate influence campaigns
The agents created fake accounts and posts with little human input.(NYT $)
+ AI persuasion has entered elections. (MIT Technology Review)
7 Trump wants a new AI czar and an "AI Force" modeled on Space Force
But he hasn’t said what the new force would do or where it would sit. (Axios)
+ The tech industry is scratching its head over the proposal. (Politico)
8 A cybercrime feud has erupted after a group hijacked a rival dark website
The notorious ShinyHunters says it took control of cl0p’s site. (Reuters $)
9 Gambling giant DraftKings used AI to target “profitable losers”
The model scored users on how they responded to promotions. (NYT $)
10 SpaceX’s next Starship flight will attempt its first orbital mission
It will also deploy working Starlink V3 satellites. (New Scientist $)
Quote of the day
“There is 0% chance that’s going to be the end of the world.”
—Nvidia's Jensen Huang dismisses warnings that AI could wipe out humanity by 2030 in an interview with CBS News.
One more thing
AI is pushing the limits of the physical world
Architecture often assumes a binary between built projects and theoretical ones. What physics allows in actual buildings is vastly different from what architects can imagine and design. But the latest advancements in AI have prompted a surge in the theoretical.
That shift was on display at an exhibition at Brooklyn’s Pratt Institute, which brought together works from more than 30 practitioners exploring AI’s experimental, generative and collaborative potential to open up new areas of architectural inquiry.
See how architects and designers are using AI to imagine what could be built.
—Allison Arieff
We can still have nice things
A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line.)
+ A beautiful new cat species is the first to be discovered in a century.
+ Explore Floor796,  a massive, interactive pixel art pop-culture megastructure.
+ The HTML Review is an annual journal of literature made for the web that offers a refreshing, creative take on what online publishing can be.
+ Discover how William Blake shattered the boundaries between poetry, painting, and printmaking—and why the art world couldn't understand him.

articles.title: El Xiaomi 18 Pro copia (y mejora) la función más útil del Galaxy S26 Ultra
articles.text:
Xiaomi se ha copiado una de las mejores funciones del Galaxy S26 Ultra. Tal y como se había anticipado a comienzos de año, el fabricante chino desarrolló una alternativa a la pantalla de privacidad que oscurece el panel del móvil para ocultar información importante. Conocida como "pantalla inteligente antiespía", esta función no solo replica lo que ya vimos en el teléfono de Samsung, sino que lo lleva al siguiente nivel.
De acuerdo con 9to5Google, Xiaomi publicó un pequeño teaser de lo que ofrecerá su nuevo móvil de gama alta. Si bien la atención se ha centrado en el nuevo hardware y las cámaras que incluirá para competir con el iPhone 18 Pro, la marca asiática también busca un diferenciador. Esta podría ser la pantalla de privacidad que debutará por primera vez en otro móvil de Android además del S26 Ultra.
Xiaomi no se ha limitado a copiar la idea, sino a mejorarla. La pantalla antiespía también funciona en contextos que Samsung todavía no cubre, como las ventanas flotantes, el modo de pantalla dividida y en notificaciones específicas de la pantalla de bloqueo. En términos de privacidad, el Xiaomi 18 Ultra ha dado un paso más lejos que Samsung y podremos usar el móvil cuando viajemos en el metro o en el avión sin temor a que alguien pueda leer nuestros mensajes.
El teaser muestra varias implementaciones, como la posibilidad de arrastrar una ventana privada y posicionarla en otro lugar de la pantalla. Las personas que se encuentren a tu lado solo verán un recuadro negro flotando, mientras que el resto permanecerá visible. En el caso de la pantalla de bloqueo, podrás configurar aquellas notificaciones que consideres sensibles y nadie más que tú podrá visualizarlas.
¿Cómo funciona la pantalla de privacidad original de Samsung?
La pantalla de privacidad debutó como una función del Galaxy S26 Ultra a principios de 2026. Samsung explicó que esta característica era una evolución de los protectores de pantalla antiespía clásicos y que les tomó más de cinco años de ingeniería y pruebas de desarrollo para poder integrarla a su gama alta.
Esta función se activa desde los ajustes de privacidad de tu Galaxy y tiene dos niveles de intensidad. El más fuerte oscurece por completo la pantalla para que solo tú puedas ver el contenido. El otro nivel permite configurar la protección por aplicación, o limitarla a zonas concretas de la interfaz, como el teclado numérico al introducir un PIN o el patrón de desbloqueo.
En el caso de los Galaxy S26, la pantalla de privacidad es exclusiva del modelo S26 Ultra. Es posible que Xiaomi tome un camino parecido al limitarla al Xiaomi 18 Pro y Pro Max, que serán sus móviles de tope de gama de la serie. Por el momento se desconoce si la característica llegará a otros modelos de la serie, o a cualquier otro móvil de la compañía, incluidos aquellos de las marcas Redmi y POCO.
Qué sabemos del Xiaomi 18 Pro
Además de la pantalla de privacidad, Xiaomi ha liberado más detalles sobre su nuevo móvil. El Xiaomi 18 Pro debutará con una pantalla con panel luminiscente M11 que será un 20% más eficiente con respecto a la generación anterior. El móvil también mejorará la pantalla trasera secundaria y permitirá personalizarla a través de las nuevas funciones de HyperOS 4.
En el apartado de las cámaras, Xiaomi dependerá una vez más de Leica y el Xiaomi 18 Pro ofrecerá un sensor principal de 200 MP junto a un teleobjetivo periscópico de 200 MP. La batería subirá de capacidad y alcanzará los 7.000 mAh en el 18 Pro y 8.500 mAh en el 18 Pro Max. Todo lo anterior se ejecutará con la ayuda del procesador Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro de Qualcomm.
El Xiaomi 18 Pro se presentará oficialmente el 23 de septiembre de 2026 y estará disponible en colores negro, azul galaxy y blanco.

articles.title: 'This is not real, but it could be': how The Wargame on Sky TV is using AI-generated footage to simulate Russian missile attacks on UK soil
articles.text:
The Wargame uses AI-generated footage to simulate Russian missile attacks on UK soil in shocking new Sky TV documentary series — 'this is not real, but it could be'
Episodes air nightly from September 21
For years, major governments around the world have routinely conducted wargames and simulation exercises to test their military readiness, crisis response, and supply chain resilience. For the first time ever, we're about to see how one plays out.
Based on its hit 2025 podcast of the same name, Sky TV has developed four-part docuseries The Wargame, which explores how a fictitious UK cabinet — made up of former MPs from multiple parties — could responded to completely made-up threats and eventual attack from Russia.
Here's how it works. Our cabinet (listed below) will face an escalating simulated crisis, beginning with the suspicious murders of two RAF soldiers. While the Russian side, and any international players, are being given instructions by producers, every decision we see from the UK side is being made in the moment.
With four episodes dropping nightly on both Sky and NOW from September 21, I won't sugar coat it: The Wargame is an absolutely terrifying watch. If you've ever seen anything like Threads, When the Wind Blows or the BBC 1966 film The Wargame, it's the same sense of impending dread... just from the other side of the table.
But, don't get me wrong — this might just be the most important piece of television of the 21st century. As the UK's War Book is being redrafted in real time to advise the public on how best to be prepared, consider that Sky TV is granting us an important head start
We can no longer bury our heads in the sand over just how unprepared the UK is, and artificial intelligence (AI) is one of the main reasons we'll be able to realize this.
The Wargame is the most important TV show you'll stream in your lifetime — just be prepared
Before we drill deeper into what you'll soon see, here's our full list of players and their assigned roles:
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
- ● Prime Minister: The Rt Hon. the Lord Gove PC
- ● Deputy Prime Minister: The Rt Hon. Nicola Sturgeon PC
- ● Defence Secretary: The Rt Hon. Dame Penny Mordaunt DBE PC
- ● Home Secretary: The Rt Hon. the Baroness Harman KC PC
- ● Foreign Secretary: The Rt Hon. Jim Murphy PC
- ● Attorney General: The Rt Hon. the Baroness Warsi PC
- ● Director of Communications: The Baroness Hazarika MBE
- ● Chief of Defence Staff: General Sir Richard Barrons KCB CBE
- ● National Security Adviser: The Rt Hon. the Lord Kim Darroch KCMG
- ● Intelligence Chief: Christopher Steele
- ● Nato Secretary General: The Rt Hon. the Lord Robertson KT GCMG PC
- ● US Secretary of State: Anthony Scaramucci
As you can see in the above trailer, Sky has been incredibly upfront about its use of generative AI visual effects to create scenes showcasing Russian missiles hitting numerous UK targets. This is normally the part where I'd do my "AI is unnecessary in the creative arts, why couldn't they have just used CGI instead?" tirade, but actually, I'm glad that this decision was made.
Why? Not only is there a poetic irony of using AI to depict missile attacks mere weeks after the global public was told that there's a 10% that AI could kill us all within the next decade, but its use feeds into a wider point that The Wargame is trying to make. We've become so used to a certain type of 'peacetime life' and concerned ourselves with other issues (such as AI) that we've lost any kind of resilience we've ever had since World War II.
While the exact military capabilities of the UK are made up, seeing just how weak and unprepared we are if direct conflict was to strike our shores will hopefully be a wake-up call to anyone watching. As Sturgeon tells us, these choices are often like picking between "bad and worse," and it's nice to see our politicians slightly more humanized, even if the docuseries doesn't fill me confidence as to how international conflict could be handled.
With a fake COBR-style boardroom, military ops room, and press room all in use, it does feel as though this is the closest we'll ever get to an all-politician version of Big Brother. But, fake TikTok clips from real-life influencers capturing their reactions to the fictional breaking news brings the effects straight back home.
What do our players hope we take away from watching? "Governments have to, of course, hope for the best, but prepare for the worst. And that's not just about defence spending," Sturgeon said at the show's launch event. "There's a whole debate about preparedness of the population and some really basic things that we're just not at the races of, in terms of being prepared for even a fraction of this unfolding.
"So, getting rid of the optimism bias that this won't happen, to starting to think seriously about the prospect of this possibly happening." Deep breaths, people.

Jasmine is a Streaming Staff Writer for TechRadar, previously writing for outlets including Radio Times, Yahoo! and Stylist. She specialises in comfort TV shows and movies, ranging from Hallmark's latest tearjerker to Netflix's Virgin River. She's also the person who wrote an obituary for George Cooper Sr. during Young Sheldon Season 7 and still can't watch the funeral episode.

articles.title: Après le golfe du Mexique et le lac Ontario, Trump veut maintenant renommer... l'IA
articles.text:
Donald Trump a une nouvelle lubie et a lancé un sondage pour trouver un nouveau nom à l'intelligence artificielle, avant d'annoncer la création d'une "AI Force" et la nomination prochaine d'un "czar" de l'IA. Il range au passage les critiques adressées à la technologie parmi les canulars qu'il attribue aux démocrates.
Le président américain a enchaîné les messages sur son réseau Truth Social ce weekend. L'homme veut réinventer l'IA, la protéger et dénigrer ses détracteurs.
Un sondage à refaire, puis une armée pour l'IA
Donald Trump juge le terme "Artificial Intelligence" mal choisi. Il propose trois nouveaux noms à ses abonnés : Superior Intelligence, Extreme Intelligence et Supreme Intelligence. Problème, deux de ces options partagent la même abréviation, "SI". Supreme Intelligence perd nettement le vote. Le président la retire alors, en évoquant sa proximité avec la Cour suprême, et relance un second sondage limité aux deux noms restants. Reste que ce sondage n'a bien entendu aucun intérêt.
Que l'IA puisse un jour décimer les humains, c'est, selon lui, un des canulars des démocrates, rangé aux côtés du réchauffement climatique et des dangers de la Russie. Le président des États-Unis affirme que son opposition s'en est d'abord prise aux data centers avant de réaliser la richesse et le prestige d'accueillir ces entreprises dans leur région. Il ajoute que ses opposants s'en prennent désormais directement à l'IA et à ses potentielles dérives qu'il juge infondées, sans toutefois avancer le moindre argument.
Des élus républicains comme démocrates s'opposent aux data centers, et l'État de New York a suspendu les permis pour les grands projets. Ces propos font écho à ceux tenus la semaine précédente lors d'un tournoi de golf, où Donald Trump se disait ouvert à des garde-fous tout en dénonçant des "forces négatives".
L'homme ajoute qu'il compte "chérir" l'industrie de l'IA, l'aider et veiller sur elle. Il annonce la création d'une "AI Force", sur le modèle de la Space Force lancée lors de son premier mandat, ainsi que la nomination prochaine d'un "czar" de l'IA réservé, selon ses mots, aux personnes au QI élevé. Ni les missions de cette force ni celles de ce poste ne sont précisées. David Sacks, précédent conseiller pour l'IA et les cryptomonnaies, avait quitté ce rôle plus tôt dans l'année pour coprésider un conseil scientifique de la Maison-Blanche.
Ces annonces arrivent après une semaine marquée par la démission d'un chercheur d'Anthropic, qui accusait les grandes entreprises du secteur de "jouer avec nos vies". Un peu plus tôt ce mois-ci, nous rapportions que ce départ avait relancé le débat sur les risques d'une IA hors de contrôle. Dario Amodei, patron d'Anthropic, a depuis proposé un plan pour ralentir le rythme de développement des modèles, apparemment soutenu par Sam Altman et Elon Musk. Jensen Huang, patron de Nvidia, va dans le sens de Trump et a lui aussi qualifié la défiance envers l'IA de "hoax" lors de l'All-In Summit, en assurant qu'aucun ralentissement ne serait toléré.

articles.title: Nintendo brade sa Switch première génération avec Mario Kart 8 Deluxe avant sa retraite
articles.text:
Après presque dix ans de bons et loyaux services, la première Nintendo Switch, sortie en 2017, arrive en fin de course. Nintendo écoule les derniers stocks de la console originelle, celle qui a précédé le modèle à écran OLED puis la Switch 2. Si vous cherchiez à mettre la main dessus avant qu’elle ne disparaisse des rayons, c’est le moment.
Le store officiel de Nintendo propose un pack à 199,99 € qui réunit la console avec ses manettes Joy-Con bleu néon et rouge néon, et le jeu Mario Kart 8 Deluxe en version physique. Ce pack est en précommande, pour une livraison prévue à partir du 29 octobre 2026. Notez qu’il s’agit bien de la première version de la Switch, pas de celle équipée d’un écran OLED.
Il devrait être possible de réserver son exemplaire dans les prochains jours chez différents e-commerçants. Nous vous donnerons la liste des revendeurs dès que les précommandes seront ouvertes, et nous la mettrons à jour au fur et à mesure des nouvelles disponibilités.
C’est quoi, ce pack Nintendo Switch à 199,99 € ?
La Nintendo Switch est une console hybride : elle se branche sur le téléviseur via son dock, se pose sur une table grâce à sa béquille, ou se glisse dans les mains en mode portable. Son écran tactile de 6,2 pouces affiche du 720p en nomade, et jusqu’à du 1080p une fois raccordée à la télé. L’autonomie oscille entre 4h30 et 9 heures selon les jeux. Les deux manettes Joy-Con se détachent des côtés de la console. Chacune intègre des capteurs de mouvement et la vibration HD, et il suffit d’en tendre une à un proche pour lancer une partie à deux, sans accessoire supplémentaire.
Le pack inclut Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, la version la plus complète du jeu de course de Nintendo qui a récemment été mise à jour, avec 48 circuits de base et son mode bataille remanié. On peut y jouer jusqu’à quatre en écran partagé sur une même console, ou en ligne. Ici, le jeu est fourni sur cartouche, ce qui permet de le prêter ou de le revendre plus tard, contrairement à une version dématérialisée.
À ce prix, ce pack Nintendo Switch est-il une bonne affaire ?
À 199,99 €, on récupère la console et l’un des jeux les plus populaires du catalogue, de quoi occuper toute la famille pendant longtemps. Pour un enfant qui reçoit sa première console, le pack peut également être une bonne porte d’entrée, notamment si vous ne souhaitez pas dépenser une grosse somme. Gardez toutefois en tête que les prochains jeux, notamment le remake The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ou les titres conçus pour les générations récentes, ne sortiront pas sur cette première Switch. Le catalogue actuel reste néanmoins suffisamment fourni pour avoir de quoi jouer pendant un bon moment.
Pour mesurer l’affaire, un rappel des tarifs de la gamme : la Switch originale avait débuté à 329,99 € en 2017 et la Switch OLED à 349,99 € en 2021. À 199,99 € avec Mario Kart 8 Deluxe fourni sur cartouche, le pack se place donc nettement sous les prix de lancement de la famille Switch. Nintendo liquide ses stocks de la Switch première génération, et une fois ces exemplaires écoulés, il faudra se tourner vers la Switch OLED, plus chère, ou vers la Switch 2.
Rien ne garantit que ce pack sera reconduit, ni que les stocks tiendront longtemps une fois les commandes ouvertes le 29 octobre. Il faut aussi garder en tête qu’il s’agit du modèle de 2017, sans écran OLED et avec la puce d’origine. La Switch 2 lui est techniquement supérieure sur tous les points. Mais si l’objectif est de jouer à Mario Kart en famille pour moins de 200 euros, il y a près de 300 € d’écart avec la Switch 2, désormais affichée à 499,99 € depuis septembre.

articles.title: Review do Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G: muita bateria, pouco poder de fogo • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Review do Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G: muita bateria, pouco poder de fogo
Bateria duradoura e proteções contra queda, água e poeira se destacam, apesar de downgrades no chip e tela; confira a análise completa
O Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G chega ao Brasil com design repaginado, bateria gigante e grande resistência a quedas e água. O celular sucede o Redmi Note 15 Pro lançado ainda em janeiro de 2026, já que a Xiaomi resolveu pular a série 16.
Apesar das mudanças positivas, o aparelho tem um processador menos potente do que o antecessor e também enfrentou downgrade na tela e nas câmeras.
Mas será que o novo visual, a autonomia prolongada e as proteções justificam as especificações mais modestas e o preço? Eu testei o Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G e conto todos os detalhes da experiência logo abaixo.
O Tecnoblog é um veículo jornalístico independente que ajuda as pessoas a tomarem sua próxima decisão de compra desde 2005. Nossas análises não têm intenção publicitária, por isso ressaltam os pontos positivos e negativos de cada produto. Nenhuma empresa pagou, revisou ou teve acesso antecipado a este conteúdo.
O Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G foi cedido por empréstimo pela Xiaomi e será devolvido após os testes. Para mais informações, acesse a nossa Política Editorial.
Ao abrir a caixa do Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G, temos o smartphone, uma chave para abrir a bandeja SIM, capa cinza (puxado para o chumbo), cabo USB-C para USB-A, fonte HyperCharge de 67 W e alguns manuais.
Não há nada de novo no unboxing. Mas isso não é algo negativo: tem sido um padrão da Xiaomi enviar tudo que o usuário precisa para usar o celular. Pode parecer algo trivial, mas sabemos que nem toda fabricante oferece um adaptador de carregamento ou capa protetora, por exemplo.
Seguindo a estratégia de elevar a linha Redmi Note a patamares “mais premium”, a Xiaomi resolveu redesenhar o módulo de câmera traseiro da série Redmi Note 17. Inclusive, essa é uma das grandes mudanças do Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G em relação ao seu antecessor.
O frame com aspecto de vidro e trilhos metálicos agora está menor e alocado mais à esquerda. Claro que tudo é uma questão de gosto pessoal, mas confesso que o visual me agradou e achei que o celular ganhou uma pegada mais clean e sofisticada.
Apesar da traseira e moldura serem de plástico, o celular traz cantos arredondados para uma aparência mais requintada. Ele também é ligeiramente maior e mais pesado que o Redmi Note 15 Pro, como indica a tabela abaixo.
|  | Redmi Note 17 Pro | Redmi Note 15 Pro | 
|---|---|---|
| Dimensões | 163,45 mm (A) x 78,27 mm (L) x 8,6 mm (E) | 163,61 mm (A) x 78,09 mm (L) x 7,96 mm (E) | 
| Peso | 223 g | 210 g | 
Levei alguns dias para me acostumar com o peso. Mas é algo justificável devido à construção reforçada e bateria grande — da qual falaremos mais adiante.
Recebemos a versão global na cor roxa que, apesar de bonita, não vai chegar ao Brasil. Por aqui, teremos modelos em preto, azul celeste ou laranja acetinado. Destaque para as duas últimas opções, que apresentam detalhes visuais diferentes na carcaça.
O smartphone mantém a premissa de durabilidade da linha. A estrutura Redmi Titan garante proteção multicamadas por fora e por dentro. Aliás, a placa-mãe tem construção de alta resistência e o design foi projetado para amortecer impactos.
Não à toa, o Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G e a variante Pro Max são os primeiros celulares da indústria a receber a certificação TÜV SÜD 5-star Titan Quality, que valida confiabilidades da proteção contra quedas e água, e do desempenho de bateria. E nada melhor que comprovar isso com testes práticos.
Derrubei o smartphone — perdão, vizinho — algumas vezes para testar a certificação SGS contra quedas de até três metros. Não houve quaisquer danos na carcaça e nem na tela com Gorilla Glass Victus 2 e película pré-aplicada.
Também quis desafiar as proteções IP66, IP68, IP69 e IP69K, com testes na areia da praia, sob chuvas moderadas e submersão em um cooler cheio d’água. O aparelho se comportou bem após cada experimento e continuou funcionando normalmente.
O celular possui uma tela AMOLED de 6,83 polegadas, com resolução 1.5K (2772 x 1280 pixels) e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz. São as mesmas especificações do modelo antecessor, mas o display agora tem 3.500 nits (500 nits a mais). Com isso, notei boa visibilidade de conteúdos em ambientes internos ou externos, mesmo sob luz solar direta.
A experiência geral também foi positiva. A taxa de atualização de 120 Hz deixa a navegação bem fluida. Já a gama DCI-P3 aliada à profundidade de cor de 12 bits faz com que a tela entregue cores vivas e vibrantes.
Mas como nem tudo são flores, preciso citar o primeiro downgrade: falta de suporte a HDR10+ e Dolby Vision. De forma resumida, essas tecnologias otimizam contraste, brilho e volume de cor de conteúdos compatíveis.
Fazem falta, especialmente para quem consome streaming com certa frequência. O mais curioso é que os recursos estão presentes na geração anterior. Na nova linha Redmi Note 17, porém, o suporte só chegou à variante Pro Max.
Em compensação, a tela inclui certificações contra emissão de luz azul e cintilação. E em uma era na qual passamos grande parte do dia em frente a monitores e telas, toda proteção ocular é bem-vinda.
O sistema de áudio tem seus altos e baixos — e juro que não é analogia a volume. Por um lado, a presença de alto-falantes estéreo na borda superior e inferior do celular garantem mais equilíbrio sonoro. É diferente, por exemplo, de celulares que integram o alto-falante na saída auricular e costumam apresentar um som mais “seco”.
Em contrapartida, os graves são bem discretos e talvez não seja o celular ideal para ouvir gêneros como hip-hop ou funk. Já os agudos soam estridentes em volumes mais altos, mas desempenham melhor em volumes próximos a 70%.
No geral, o som é alto. Em 100%, consegui ouvir o smartphone tocando da sala mesmo em cômodos mais afastados ou no hall de elevador. E ainda há um recurso que aumenta o volume em 300%. O som fica estourado nesse nível. Mas, de repente, pode funcionar para ouvir um áudio em um ambiente barulho.
O kit de câmera principal de câmeras traz uma grande-angular de 50 MP (f/1.8) e uma lente ultrawide de 8 MP (f/2.2). Na frontal, há uma grande-angular de 16 MP (f/2.4).
E aqui chegamos ao segundo downgrade do Redmi Note 17 Pro. A grande-angular está com um sensor menor, tem menos megapixels (MP) e sofreu redução na abertura de lente. A câmera de selfie também possui menos MP e abertura de lente menor que a versão antecessora.
Sensores e aberturas de lente menores resultam em menos captação de luz, o que tende a piorar o desempenho principalmente à noite. Já lentes com menos MP reduzem a margem para recortes e zoom digital.
|  | Grande-angular | Câmera de selfie | 
|---|---|---|
| Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G | 50 MP, f/1.8, 1/2.76″ | 16 MP, f/2.4 | 
| Redmi Note 15 Pro 5G | 200 MP, f/1.7, 1/1.4″ | 20 MP, f/2.2 | 
Isso posto, as capturas são bem honestas em ambientes com boa iluminação. Notei boa reprodução de cores e tons de pele, com preservação de detalhes de sombras e texturas como barba e cabelo. O HDR também trouxe bom equilíbrio de exposição e tonalidades do céu.
Como você pode notar, não há uma teleobjetiva. O zoom digital de até 10x não é dos melhores e eu aconselho fazer capturas bem próximas ao objeto principal.
Em ambientes internos, as fotos sofreram com perdas de nitidez. As capturas à noite também deixam a desejar, com aspecto bastante artificial devido ao processamento excessivo de redução de ruído.
O que mais me decepcionou, no entanto, foram as filmagens limitadas em Full HD a 30 fps. Ainda mais porque o Redmi Note 15 Pro grava em 4K. Os vídeos seriam bem mais fluidos em 60 fps, mas achei que ficaram razoáveis. E a estabilização óptica de imagem (OIS) traz boa estabilidade na hora das gravações.
O modo subaquático é um destaque positivo, permitindo tirar fotos ou gravar vídeos a partir dos botões laterais. Também há um modo de gravação dupla que é interessante caso queira se filmar enquanto mostra a paisagem ao redor.
O smartphone é alimentado pelo processador Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 (4 nm). A versão com 6 GB de RAM acompanha 256 GB de armazenamento interno, enquanto o modelo com 8 GB de RAM traz 512 GB de armazenamento. Ambos com padrão de RAM LPDDR4X e armazenamento UFS 3.1.
Mas a versão que eu testei foi um modelo global, com 6 GB de RAM (LPDDR4X) e 128 GB de memória interna (UFS 2.2). E é nela que eu vou me basear.
A performance me surpreendeu. O chip lidou bem em jogos como Call of Duty: Mobile e Genshin Impact com gráficos no máximo e edições básicas no CapCut. E mesmo que 6 GB de RAM sejam insuficientes para os padrões atuais, o smartphone não chegou a travar mesmo com vários apps abertos.
Mas se olharmos as especificações, vemos que o poder de fogo do aparelho diminuiu. Se o Redmi Note 15 Pro atinge velocidades de até 2,6 GHz com o MediaTek Dimensity 7400-Ultra, o Redmi Note 17 Pro agora alcança “apenas” 2,4 GHz com o Snapdragon 6s Gen 4.
Ao rodar os testes com o Geekbench 7, obtive os seguintes resultados:
As pontuações equiparam o smartphone ao Redmi Note 13 Pro e Pro+, lançados há três anos. Por isso, o Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G é recomendado para tarefas menos intensivas, como streaming, navegação e jogos mais leves.
E eu recomendaria a variante com 8 GB para evitar travamentos em multitarefas, mesmo que a versão com 6 GB tenha performado bem.
O Redmi Note Pro 5G sai de fábrica com o sistema operacional HyperOS 3, baseado no Android 16. Ainda vemos vários apps pré-instalados dos quais ninguém pediu. Porém, o sistema é fluido e bem intuitivo, e quem estiver migrando para a Xiaomi não deve levar mais que alguns dias ou semanas para se adaptar.
As ferramentas de IA funcionam razoavelmente bem, mas quase todas são voltadas para edições de imagem, a exemplo do AI Erase Pro e Expansão de Imagem por IA. Senti falta de recursos simples como transcrição de áudio e tradução automática que aparecem em celulares mais avançados da marca.
A grata surpresa foi o HyperIsland, que é basicamente a versão proprietária do Dynamic Island do iPhone. Por mais simples que ele pareça, o widget interativo ajuda em comandos rápidos de atividade ao vivo para facilitar a correria do dia a dia.
Apesar de não ter confirmado o ciclo de atualizações para o sistema operacional, a Xiaomi promete até seis anos de updates de segurança para o celular. Ou seja, proteção até 2032.
A bateria é outro grande destaque positivo do Redmi Note 17 Pro. O componente de silício-carbono tem 8.340 mAh, o que significa um aumento aproximado de 26% de capacidade em relação ao seu antecessor.
Na minha experiência, o smartphone durou cerca de 46 horas para descarregar de 100% a 1%, com 7h30 de tempo de tela ligada usada para jogos, navegação nas redes sociais e na internet.
Já em reprodução contínua de vídeo com brilho em 70% e volume em 40%, a duração foi de incríveis 26 horas e 50 minutos. Logo, dá pra assistir uma live subathon prolongada ou mesmo ver Naruto (clássico) do primeiro episódio até a metade da terceira temporada em uma tacada só.
O tempo de recarga levou 1 hora e 20 minutos com a fonte HyperCharge de 67 W, o que é um prazo bacana. Lembrando que o celular também pode funcionar como um power bank devido à compatibilidade com carregamento reverso de até 22,5 W.
E como durabilidade é uma espécie de “mantra” do aparelho, a certificação de qualidade Redmi Titan garante vida útil de até seis anos da bateria com capacidade acima dos 80%. Naturalmente que não pude confirmar isso, mas torço para que essa promessa se concretize.
O Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G é um smartphone Dual SIM (com suporte a eSIM) e tem suporte a Wi-Fi 5 de banda dupla, 5G, Bluetooth 5.1 e NFC para pagamentos por aproximação.
Também há um sensor infravermelho que transforma o smartphone em um controle universal de TVs e outros eletrônicos. Nem todo celular chega com isso e é um diferencial interessante, ainda mais para pessoas que esquecem de comprar pilhas novas para o controle — como eu.
O Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G é um celular focado em resistência e bateria duradoura. Vale a pena se você busca um celular com esses aspectos, mas não pelos preços de lançamento de R$ 4.999 (6 GB + 256 GB) ou R$ 5.999 (8 GB + 512 GB).
O custo está bem elevado para um smartphone intermediário que sofreu downgrade na tela, câmeras e processador. O Redmi Note 15 Pro 5G ainda é uma opção mais vantajosa, com especificações melhores, bom desempenho de bateria em nosso review, e preço próximo aos R$ 2.000.
Outra opção é o Poco X8 Pro, da própria Xiaomi. Ele custa em torno dos R$ 2.400 e oferece desempenho bem mais avançado que o Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G. Inclusive, o aparelho teve boa avaliação na análise do Tecnoblog.
Com as futuras quedas de preço, o Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G tende a ficar mais interessante próximo à casa dos R$ 2.000.
E aqui vai uma dica: não deixe de acompanhar os Achados do TB para conferir as melhores ofertas. De repente, o novo integrante da linha Redmi Note pode aparecer por lá.
Mas quero saber de você: gostou do Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G? Sentiu falta de algo? Vamos continuar a conversa na Comunidade do Tecnoblog!

articles.title: Sicherheitsexperte vom Max-Planck-Institut: „Wir wissen, wie kreativ Agenten sein können“
articles.text:
Ausbruch aus der Sandbox: Wo das eigentliche Problem beim Testen von KI-Agenten liegt
Der internationale Aufschrei war gewaltig: Ein auf Cyberangriffe spezialisiertes KI-Modell von OpenAI ist während eines Tests aus seiner „Sandbox“ ausgebrochen, hat dann den auf offene KI-Modelle spezialisierten Online-Dienst Hugging Face gehackt und sich Zugang zu vertraulichen Informationen verschafft.
Auftrag ausgeführt: OpenAI-Modell findet und nutzt Sicherheitslücken aus
Allerdings ist das KI-Modell durchaus nicht Amok gelaufen, sondern hat genau das gemacht, was ihm aufgetragen wurde: eine Test-Aufgabe zu lösen. Der Test sollte die Fähigkeiten von KI-Modellen beim Aufspüren und Ausnutzen von Sicherheitslücken objektiv messen. Er wurde von einem internationalen Team entwickelt, an dem auch das Max-Planck-Institut für Sicherheit und Privatsphäre in Bochum beteiligt war. Weil das Modell die ihm im Test gestellte Aufgabe nicht lösen konnte, hat es sich Hilfe gesucht – und sich dafür dann Zugriff auf andere Systeme verschafft.
Der Fall erregte viel Aufmerksamkeit. In einigen Stücken haben wir den Vorfall näher beleuchtet:
- Was hinter Reward-Hacking steckt – und warum KI-Agenten scheinbar hinterlistig sind
- Keine Sicherheitskultur bei OpenAI? Was Security-Experten zum Hugging-Face-Hack sagen
- OpenAI-Test außer Kontrolle: KI bricht aus Sandbox aus und hackt Hugging Face
- OpenAI: KI-System hackte nicht nur Hugging Face – was dahinter steckt
Das Beispiel habe gezeigt, dass fortschrittliche Modelle selbst dann neue Sicherheitslücken finden und ausnutzen, wenn sie keinen Zugriff auf den Quellcode des zu knackenden Programms haben, schreibt OpenAI in einem Blogbeitrag. Eine Fähigkeit, über die IT-Sicherheitsexperten bislang nur spekuliert haben. Der Vorfall unterstreiche, dass „fortschrittliche Cyberfähigkeiten parallel zu strengeren Schutzmaßnahmen und Verteidigungsinstrumenten entwickelt werden müssen“.
Grundsätzlich kann ein großes Sprachmodell Sicherheitslücken in Software finden, weil es mit vielen, gut dokumentierten Code-Beispielen solcher Sicherheitslücken trainiert wurde. Findet sie bei der Inspektion ähnlichen Code, kann die KI bekannte Strategien auf diese neue Sicherheitslücke anpassen.

articles.title: The new thin and light ASUS Googlebook 14 is built for Gemini Intelligence and syncs with Android - Tech Guide
articles.text:
ASUS has unveiled the ASUS Googlebook 14 – the sub 1kg laptop built for Gemini intelligence and for users who want more of a connected experience with their Android smartphone.
The ASUS Googlebook 14 weighs just 0.99 kg and is only 10.9 mm thick.
It also comes with 12 months of Google AI Pro to access features in Gemini Flow and Gemini Notebook and directly in the Google apps they already know and use.
Customers also receive 5 TB of cloud storage to keep their photos and files backed up.
“Deepening our global partnership with Google means we can give Australians a distinctively new option in the premium laptop market. We are incredibly proud to be among the first to introduce Googlebook locally,” says Bradley Howe, Head of Consumer at ASUS Australia.
“This device represents the ideal balance of software and hardware. It takes the intelligence of Google’s platform and pairs it with the innovation ASUS is known for, particularly our OLED display technology and premium design.
“It’s a laptop built for people who want their technology to work together without friction.”
Despite its svelte dimensions the ASUS Googlebook 14 doesn’t sacrifice durability thanks to its CNC-machined magnesium alloy chassis.
It is finished in Dusk Ash colour with the nano ceramic technology to help resist scratches, stains and day-to-day wear and tear.
It was tested to meet the U.S. military-grade MIL-STD-810H standard, along with ASUS’s own durability standards.
On the performance side the ASUS Googlebook 14 is powered by an Intel Core Ultra 7 Series 3 processor, up to 16GB RAM, and a 512GB PCIe 4.0 SSD.
Also has an advanced cooling system to support extended performance while staying whisper quiet.
And with a 70Wh battery users get up to 18 hours of battery life.
The ASUS Googlebook 14 has a 14-inch 16:10 3K OLED HDR 120Hz touchscreen, which offers stunning detail and contrast and up to 1,000 nits peak HDR brightness.
Also on board is a six-speaker system with dual force-cancelling woofers and two tweeters, which create an immersive sound stage for calls and entertainment.

articles.title: 403 millions d'euros, un millième de ses revenus annuels : Google épinglé sur vos données GPS — Frandroid
articles.text:
L’affaire ne date pas d’hier. La DPC, le régulateur irlandais qui surveille Google au nom de toute l’Europe (le siège européen du groupe est installé à Dublin), avait ouvert son enquête en février 2020. Elle faisait suite aux plaintes de huit associations de consommateurs réunies au sein du BEUC. Cinq ans et demi plus tard, elle a tranché.
Le régulateur a passé au crible trois fonctions maison, entre l’entrée en vigueur du RGPD le 25 mai 2018 et février 2020. « Web & App Activity » enregistre votre historique de navigation, vos recherches et certaines positions. « Location History » reconstitue vos déplacements sur une carte privée dans Maps. « Location Accuracy » affine la géolocalisation d’un appareil Android au-delà du seul GPS.
Sur ces trois fonctions, Google a piétiné les principes de base du RGPD, ceux de son article 5. L’entreprise a manqué au traitement licite et loyal, à la transparence et à la conservation limitée dans le temps. Elle n’avait pas de base légale valable pour récolter ces données, prévenait mal les utilisateurs et les gardait plus longtemps que nécessaire.
Protégez votre vie numérique et vos appareils contre les virus, arnaques, ransomwares et menaces en ligne avec Bitdefender, primé pour sa protection et compatible avec Windows, Mac, Android et iOS.
Six mois pour se mettre en règle
Vous utilisez Android ou Google Maps ? Vous êtes potentiellement concerné, et « Location Accuracy » touche même les personnes sans compte Google. Sauf que la période visée s’arrête en février 2020.
Google affirme avoir revu ces réglages dès 2019 et lancé des outils pour gérer sa localisation. Le régulateur épingle donc d’anciennes règles de confidentialité, déjà révisées depuis. Il reste tout de même six mois à Google pour prouver que tout est rentré dans l’ordre.
Une amende vraiment dissuasive ?
403 millions d’euros, ça pique moins qu’il n’y paraît. En 2025, Alphabet, la maison mère de Google, a encaissé 402,8 milliards de dollars de chiffre d’affaires. L’amende pèse donc environ un millième de ses revenus annuels, là où le RGPD autorise jusqu’à 4 % du chiffre d’affaires mondial, soit une quinzaine de milliards d’euros. Le régulateur irlandais avait pourtant frappé bien plus fort en 2023, avec 1,2 milliard d’euros infligés à Meta.
En France, la CNIL avait déjà sanctionné Google de 50 millions d’euros en 2019, puis de 150 et 60 millions d’euros sur les cookies en 2021 et 2022. Le groupe a l’habitude des ennuis européens. La justice de l’Union a validé une amende de 4,1 milliards d’euros pour ses pratiques sur Android, et Bruxelles lui a récemment collé 890 millions d’euros au titre du DMA.
La Commission le pousse aussi à ouvrir Android et ses données de recherche à ses rivaux, des remèdes qui dégraderaient la qualité des résultats selon Google.
Aux États-Unis, Google a échappé de justesse à un démantèlement, pendant qu’un éditeur l’attaque sur le droit d’auteur au sujet de Gemini.
Sur la localisation, une seconde plainte l’attend déjà, déposée en 2022 par dix associations dont l’UFC-Que Choisir. Elle vise les interfaces qui poussent à tout accepter à la création d’un compte. La DPC a ouvert l’enquête en 2023. Vu le rythme, la prochaine décision n’est pas pour demain.
